title: One readiness derivation carried into graph-editing commands
description:
Add one pure domain function that, given the issues before and after a mutation, returns the readiness corrections the dependency graph demands for the issues that mutation can affect, and give the command layer one helper that turns those corrections into mutation intents. Deletion, dependency edits and template edges derive their dependents' readiness through it inside their own plan.

## Background

- `Issue::derive_readiness_correction` (`crates/jit/src/domain/types.rs:707-716`) decides one issue: a `Backlog` issue nothing blocks is `Promote`, a `Ready` issue with an unmet dependency is `Demote` (`ReadinessCorrection`, `domain/types.rs:598`). `Issue::is_blocked` (`:666`) reads only `is_dependency_met` (`:144`) of each dependency, so a correction (which moves an issue only between the non-terminal `Backlog` and `Ready`) never changes another issue's blockedness: one pass over the projected set is complete.
- Every caller chooses its own candidate set by hand: deletion walks the deleted issue's dependents (`derive_issue_deletion`, `crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:67-150`, promotion at `:103-140`, through `derive_state_transition`), dependency edits look at the edited source only (`crates/jit/src/commands/dependency.rs:605,964`), template edges look at the edge source (`crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs:1281,1342`), `check_auto_transitions` (`commands/issue.rs:889-905`) scans every issue for promotions only, and `jit validate --fix` scans every issue in both directions.
- `jit dep rm` promotes the edited source through `derive_state_transition` (`derive_dependency_removal`, `dependency.rs:515`, promotion at `:605-639`); `jit dep add` and the reduction demote directly (`derive_reduced_graph_intents`, `dependency.rs:922`, demotion at `:964-974`).
- Template application demotes directly on edge addition (`add_captured_template_edge`, `template.rs:1209`, `:1281-1291`) and promotes directly on edge removal, bypassing graph rules (`remove_captured_template_edge`, `template.rs:1305`, `:1342-1353`).
- `derive_state_transition` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:1077`) applies graph rules to a promotion and returns `GraphBlocked` with `transition_blocked` events when one refuses it.
- Nothing states which issues a mutation can affect, so there is no single place to prove that a correction is neither missed nor applied to unrelated drift.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A pure domain function takes the issues before a mutation, the issues after it and a scope, and returns each correction as an issue id with its `ReadinessCorrection`, ordered by issue id; it reads no storage and uses `Issue::derive_readiness_correction` for each candidate. The `Affected` scope admits exactly the issues that are new, whose dependency list changed, or that directly depend on an issue whose effective terminal state changed or which was removed; the `All` scope admits every projected issue.
- [hard] REQ-02: Unit tests cover promotion on a blocker reaching `Done` or `Rejected`, demotion on a blocker leaving a terminal state, demotion on an added edge, promotion on a removed edge or a deleted blocker, and no correction for `InProgress`, `Gated`, terminal or archived dependents.
- [hard] REQ-03: A property test over generated acyclic issue sets and single edits (state change, edge add or remove, deletion) shows that applying the `Affected` corrections leaves no issue whose stored readiness disagrees with the graph, and that no correction falls outside the `Affected` set.
- [hard] REQ-04: One helper beside `derive_state_transition` in `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs` maps the pure corrections over a base and a projected issue set to mutation intents: a promotion goes through `derive_state_transition` (graph rules apply; a refused promotion records its `transition_blocked` events and its error is reported after apply), a demotion is applied directly with its state-change event.
- [hard] REQ-05: Issue deletion, `dep add`, `dep rm`, dependency reduction and template edge addition and removal obtain their dependent readiness changes only from that helper; none of them calls `derive_readiness_correction` or `should_auto_transition_to_ready` directly.
- [hard] REQ-06: For each of the three command families (deletion, dependency edits, template application) one harness test shows the dependent's correction published in the same session as the primary change, and a harness test shows that removing a template edge whose promotion a graph rule refuses leaves the dependent in `Backlog` and records `transition_blocked` (it fails on today's code, which promotes directly).

## Notes

- Behaviour change: promotion after template edge removal now passes graph rules, as deletion and `dep rm` already do (REQ-06).
- Graph-rule gating of promotions stays in the command layer; the pure function only states what the graph demands.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
- cba1bff8 already derives rejection's dependent promotions inside its own plan, through the path deletion uses; that slice is done here. Closing an issue still promotes dependents in a follow-up mutation (`check_auto_transitions`), which breaches `@/inv/derived-state-coherence` today; this issue tracks that gap.

planning.outcome: One pure domain function derives readiness corrections, and graph edits apply them through one command helper.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One pure function and one helper adopted by three local call-site families, each a substitution.

title: Every state-changing plan carries its readiness corrections and creation takes initial readiness from the derivation
description:
Make each single-issue state change, the automatic transition to `Done` and every creation path derive readiness inside its own mutation plan, delete the post-commit readiness publishers, and update the core-model documentation. Rejecting, completing or reopening an issue updates its dependents in the same redo record, and new issues take their initial `Ready` promotion from the pure derivation.

## Background

- `IssueOps::update_issue` (`crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:476`) publishes through `publish_captured_field_update` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2599`, derivation `derive_field_update` `:1279`) and then, when the issue entered a terminal state, calls `check_auto_transitions` (`issue.rs:559-561`), which lists every issue and publishes one further session per promotable dependent (`issue.rs:889-905`).
- `update_issue_state` (`issue.rs:686`) and `reject_issue` without a reason use the lifecycle `State` plan (`publish_captured_state_transition`, `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2700`; `publish_captured_lifecycle_mutation`, `:2769`) and run no cascade; `reject_issue` with a reason uses the field update (`issue.rs:707-722`) and none either. A dependent of a rejected blocker stays `Backlog`, and `jit validate` does not flag it because only demotions are violations (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:505-530`). No path demotes `Ready` dependents when an issue leaves `Done` or `Rejected`; `jit validate` then reports that stored readiness disagrees with the dependency graph.
- `auto_transition_to_done` (`issue.rs:873-886`) publishes the `AutoDone` lifecycle plan (`CapturedLifecycleMutation::AutoDone`, `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:870`; arm at `:3092-3102`) and then calls `check_auto_transitions` (`issue.rs:882`). Its callers are the manual gate pass (`pass_gate`, `crates/jit/src/commands/gate.rs:876`) and the postcheck runner (`run_postchecks`, `crates/jit/src/commands/gate_check.rs:1587`); postchecks run their checkers outside the repository lock, so the automatic Done stays its own mutation after them.
- `auto_transition_to_done` publishes through `publish_captured_auto_transition` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2747`) and `publish_captured_lifecycle_mutation` (`:2769`), which opens a preflight session and a publishing session on every attempt, so each dependent that `check_auto_transitions` promotes adds two session opens. Command tests count session opens with `SessionOpenCounter` (`crates/jit/src/commands/test_helpers.rs`), measuring a baseline run first as `crates/jit/src/commands/bulk_update.rs:1548` does.
- Remaining post-commit readiness machinery: `check_auto_transitions` (`issue.rs:889-905`) publishes one `AutoReady` session per promotable issue; its other caller is `apply_bulk_update` (`bulk_update.rs:294-295`, guarded by an `entered_terminal` flag accumulated at `:264,274`), and a unit test owns it (`test_check_auto_transitions_opens_sessions_only_for_eligible_backlog_issues`, `issue.rs:1073-1109`) that a `bulk_update.rs` comment cites (`:1530`). `auto_transition_to_ready` (`issue.rs:846`) and `auto_transition_to_backlog` (`issue.rs:863`) have no other caller once `--fix` stopped publishing per correction. `publish_captured_auto_transition` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2747-2766`) maps `Ready`, `Backlog` and `Done` to the `AutoReady`, `AutoBacklog` and `AutoDone` lifecycle variants (`:861-873`), whose arms sit at `:3066-3102`; only `AutoDone` keeps a caller. The field-update outcome carries `entered_terminal` in two structs (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:1036,1046`; set at `:1488,1504,1546,2665,2679`); once its readers are gone the fields fail clippy's dead-code check.
- `crates/jit/tests/fast_issue/readiness_coherence_tests.rs:226-271` holds a property test over dependency edits that checks only the `Ready`-but-blocked direction.
- The initial `Ready`-or-`Backlog` decision is written by hand in four places: single creation (`IssueOps::create_issue`, `issue.rs:179`, sets `Ready` at `:221-222` before `publish_issue_creation`, `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2385`, which validates the draft through `derive_write_validation` at `:2444`); template application (`project_planned_issue`, `crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs:1377-1385`, used at `:1045`, sets `Ready` unconditionally and the template's edge handling demotes afterwards; its unit test asserts the projected `Ready` at `:1681-1684`); batch creation (`crates/jit/src/commands/batch_create.rs:569-573`); and the batch finalizer pass (`finalize_delta`, `crates/jit/src/repository_state/mutation.rs:725`, state at `:812-816`), which re-derives state from whether the issue has in-batch dependencies.
- Local rules must see the final state, so the decision has to precede `derive_write_validation` (`issue.rs:211-220` explains this for single creation). The pure `readiness_corrections(base, projected, scope)` returns the `Promote` corrections for new issues under its `Affected` scope; a draft has no prior state, so its promotion is applied to the draft directly, with no state-change event and no graph-rule transition check, matching today's creation behaviour.
- The command helper from the readiness derivation maps pure readiness corrections over a base and a projected issue set to mutation intents (promotion through graph rules, direct demotion).
- `docs/concepts/core-model.md:234-239` and `:808` say promotion happens "in the same operation" through `check_auto_transitions` in `issue.rs`; `:241-244` and `:809` describe demotion.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `derive_field_update` and the lifecycle `State`, `Claim`, `Release` and `AutoDone` plans add the helper's corrections for the `Affected` scope of their own change to the plan they publish; `update_issue` and `auto_transition_to_done` no longer call `check_auto_transitions`.
- [hard] REQ-02: Harness tests show a rejected blocker (with and without a reason) leaving its only-blocked dependent `Ready` within the same session, a `Done` blocker moved back to `InProgress` demoting its `Ready` dependent to `Backlog` within the same session, and passing the last manual gate of a `Gated` issue with an otherwise unblocked dependent leaving the issue `Done` and the dependent `Ready` with the same session-open count as the identical pass with no dependent (baseline counter); each fails on today's code. The readiness property test also generates state changes of blockers into and out of `Done` and `Rejected` and asserts after each edit that no issue is `Ready` while blocked or `Backlog` while unblocked.
- [hard] REQ-03: `check_auto_transitions`, `auto_transition_to_ready`, `auto_transition_to_backlog`, the `AutoReady` and `AutoBacklog` lifecycle variants with their arms, and both `entered_terminal` fields with their assignments no longer exist; the automatic transition entry point accepts only the `Done` target; no production code path publishes a session whose only purpose is a readiness correction after another mutation committed; a harness test bulk-updates a blocker to `Done` and shows its dependent `Ready` in the blocker's own publication with no extra session (session counter), replacing the deleted unit test.
- [hard] REQ-04: Single, template and batch creation build drafts in `Backlog` and apply the readiness derivation's promotions over the captured issues plus the drafts before local-rule validation; no command assigns a draft's initial state by inspecting its dependency list, and the batch finalizer pass stamps the state the draft carries without deciding it.
- [hard] REQ-05: Harness tests show, for single, template and batch creation, that a draft with no dependencies or only terminal dependencies is created `Ready`, one with an open dependency is created `Backlog`, and a local rule keyed on `Ready` sees the created state; a template whose node depends on another node of the same application creates that node `Backlog`, validated as `Backlog`, with no `Ready`-to-`Backlog` state-change event and no `first_ready_at` (it fails today).
- [hard] REQ-06: The core-model page states that dependent readiness corrections publish in the same redo record as the change that causes them, in both directions, including rejection and leaving a terminal state, and names no internal function; other pages link to it rather than restate it (`@/charter/D-13`).

## Notes

- Behaviour change: rejection promotes dependents, and leaving a terminal state demotes `Ready` dependents (REQ-02).
- Behaviour change: a template node blocked by an edge inside the same application is today projected `Ready` (`project_planned_issue`, `template.rs:1377-1385`), validated as `Ready` (`:1063`), demoted by the template's edge handling with a `Ready`-to-`Backlog` state-change event (`:1273-1293`), and stamped with `first_ready_at` by the finalizer (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mutation.rs:765-769`). After this change it is created `Backlog`, local rules validate it as `Backlog`, and it carries no demotion event and no `first_ready_at` (REQ-05). Single and batch creation yield the same initial state as today.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

title: Validate fix derives readiness through the shared helper
description:
Make the readiness part of `jit validate --fix` use the shared readiness derivation over every projected issue, so the repair and the mutation paths decide readiness with one function.

## Background

- After the one-mutation `--fix` change, `--fix` derives all fixes from one validation capture and publishes them in one mutation; its readiness step applies `Issue::derive_readiness_correction` to the projected issue set until no correction remains, inside `crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs`. Before that change the step is `check_pending_transitions` (`validate.rs:2054-2108`), which publishes one session per correction through `auto_transition_to_ready` and `auto_transition_to_backlog` (`validate.rs:2095-2096`).
- The pure domain readiness derivation returns every correction for a base and projected set under the `All` scope in one pass (a correction never changes another issue's blockedness), and the command helper maps corrections to intents, promoting through graph rules.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The `--fix` readiness step obtains its corrections from the shared derivation with the `All` scope through the shared command helper; no loop repeating `derive_readiness_correction` until a fixpoint remains in `validate.rs`.
- [hard] REQ-02: A harness test declares a graph rule that refuses the transition to `Ready` for one issue, seeds that issue `Backlog` while unblocked, and runs `--fix`: the issue stays `Backlog`, a `transition_blocked` event names the rule, and the fix report states the refused repair. It fails before this change: the one-mutation `--fix` applies each correction from `Issue::derive_readiness_correction` directly, so the issue is promoted despite the rule.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: a readiness promotion made by `--fix` now passes graph rules; a refused one is reported, as for every other promotion (REQ-02).
- That `--fix` publishes all its repairs in one mutation is owned by the one-mutation `--fix` change this task follows; this task adds no second test of it.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: validate --fix computes readiness repairs with the shared derivation over the whole projected set.

title: One state derivation for update and lifecycle transitions
description:
Give the issue state field one derivation: `jit issue update --state` and the lifecycle transitions (`jit claim`, state changes and rejection) run the same prechecks and the same divert of `Done` to `Gated`.

## Background

- The lifecycle path runs precheck gates when a `Ready` issue moves to `InProgress` (`lifecycle_requires_prechecks`, `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:888-897`, used in the preflight of `publish_captured_lifecycle_mutation` `:2769`, at `:2798`, and rechecked at `:2915`; `captured_precheck_plan` `:659`). Checkers run in that preflight, outside the repository lock, and a strict unleased request is refused before they run (`:2840-2860`). The lifecycle path diverts `Done` with unpassed gates to `Gated` (`mod.rs:3107-3129`).
- The field path (`derive_field_update`, `mod.rs:1279`; published by `publish_captured_field_update` `:2599`), which `jit issue update --state` and bulk update use, has its own `Done`-to-`Gated` divert (`mod.rs:1388-1409`) and runs no precheck: with an automatic precheck gate whose checker fails, `jit issue update <id> --state in_progress` still moves the issue to `InProgress`.
- A unit test in `crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:3499-3509` calls `lifecycle_requires_prechecks` through `capture_mutation_preflight`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One state derivation decides a state change for both the field and the lifecycle paths: prechecks are a captured precondition of any `Ready` to `InProgress` change, run in the preflight as today, and one place diverts `Done` with unpassed gates to `Gated`.
- [hard] REQ-02: A test sets an automatic precheck gate whose checker fails on a `Ready` issue and shows `jit issue update --state in_progress` refused with the issue left `Ready`; it fails on today's code, which moves the issue.
- [hard] REQ-03: The existing lifecycle precheck, claim, lease-before-precheck and divert tests pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: `jit issue update --state in_progress` runs prechecks (in a preflight outside the repository lock, as `jit claim` does) and is refused when one fails.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: issue update --state and the lifecycle path share one state derivation with prechecks and one Done divert.

title: One field derivation for bulk, dedicated and single-issue changes
description:
Make every field change derive its issue state and events through the general field update: a bulk field change writes the same state and events as a single-issue update, and issue assign, issue unassign and gate attach and detach publish through that update, so each field change has one derivation whatever command requests it.

## Background

- The post-commit readiness machinery (`entered_terminal`, the `AutoReady` and `AutoBacklog` arms) is already removed when this task starts, and `derive_field_update` already carries its readiness corrections.
- `CapturedFieldUpdate` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:917`) carries a `bulk` flag (`:932`) that only `CapturedFieldUpdate::bulk` sets (`:951-971`); the other constructions spell `bulk: false` (`CapturedFieldUpdate::label_edit`, `mod.rs:1009-1029`, and the single-issue update in `crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:536-556`).
- A single-issue update stages gate and assignee changes through `issue_local_mutations` (`mod.rs:976-1008`), which apply through `apply_captured_issue_mutation` (`mod.rs:1606`) and emit `gate_added`/`gate_removed` per key, `issue_claimed`, and for unassign an `issue_updated` with source `issue-unassign`; gate add also inserts a `Pending` `gates_status` entry.
- With `bulk` set, `issue_local_mutations` returns nothing (`:977`) and `derive_field_update` (`mod.rs:1279`) folds the same fields inline (`:1342-1356`): gate add pushes only `gates_required` with no status entry, gate edits record `issue_updated` with `fields: ["gates"]`, and the field event uses source `bulk-update` (`:1510-1521`). The stored issue and the event log differ by invocation path. `test_bulk_transition_emits_same_events_as_single_transitions` (`crates/jit/src/commands/bulk_update.rs:1183`) covers state changes only.
- `IssueOps::assign_issue` (`issue.rs:726`), `IssueOps::unassign_issue` (`issue.rs:772`), `add_gates` (`crates/jit/src/commands/gate.rs:696`) and `remove_gates` (`gate.rs:742`) publish through `publish_captured_issue_mutation` (`mod.rs:2298`), which captures only the target issue, the event log and the gate registry and runs no local or graph rule; it also publishes `SetManualGateStatus` (`mod.rs:493`) for manual pass and fail.
- `issue update` publishes through `publish_captured_field_update` (`mod.rs:2599`), which captures the full mutation base, applies the issue-local mutations through `issue_local_mutations` (`mod.rs:976`) inside `derive_field_update`, runs write validation and checks the lease in session.
- `add_gates` and `remove_gates` return `GateAddResult { added, already_exist }` and `GateRemoveResult { removed, not_found }` from `CapturedIssueMutationOutcome` (`mod.rs:525`); callers are `crates/jit/src/main.rs:3897` (gate add), `add_gate` (`gate.rs:685`), and the tests in `gate.rs:1550-1577`, `crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:2968-2970`, `crates/jit/tests/fast_issue/bulk_operations_tests.rs` and `crates/jit/tests/fast_issue/short_hash_tests.rs:202-205`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `CapturedFieldUpdate` has no `bulk` field, no construction names it, and no event carries the source `bulk-update`; a bulk field change composes the same issue-local mutations as a single-issue update.
- [hard] REQ-02: A unit test shows bulk gate add storing a `Pending` status entry and writing one `gate_added` per key (both fail today).
- [hard] REQ-03: Assign, unassign, gate attach and gate detach publish through the general field update, and `publish_captured_issue_mutation` publishes only manual gate status changes.
- [hard] REQ-04: The commands keep their return values: gate attach reports added and already-present keys, gate detach reports removed and absent keys.
- [hard] REQ-05: One property test over an initial issue and a field change shows the dedicated command, a single-issue update and a bulk update filtered to that issue producing equal stored issues and equal event bodies, ignoring event ids and timestamps.
- [hard] REQ-06: A test shows an enforcing local rule refusing a dedicated assign that the general update refuses (today the dedicated command skips rules and succeeds).

## Notes

- Behaviour change: bulk gate and assignee edits now write the per-field events and status entries single updates write; `issue_updated` from bulk uses the `issue-update` source.
- Behaviour change: the dedicated commands now run local and graph rules and capture the full mutation base, so a rule that refuses `issue update --assignee` also refuses `issue assign`.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Bulk, dedicated and single-issue field changes share one field derivation, state and events.

title: Dedicated, gate and template writes check their leases in their publishing session
description:
Define the foreign-lease refusal once as a typed error, and move the lease checks of gate attach, remove, pass and fail, issue assign and unassign, and template application into the session that publishes their change, under a claims guard taken first. Their lock-free pre-session check is deleted.

## Background

- The one lease rule is `refuse_foreign_leases` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs`): strict mode refuses when anyone other than the writer holds an active lease on a target, warn mode answers the same findings, and off answers none; a mutation with no lease on an unleased issue succeeds. Strict mode returns its text through `anyhow::bail!`, so callers and `crates/jit/src/output/failure.rs` can match it only by string. Error types live in `crates/jit/src/errors.rs` as `thiserror` structs (for example `LeaseNotFoundError`). `crates/jit/tests/cli_repo_workflow/lease_enforcement_tests.rs` owns the rule with a table over every CLI leaf.
- Two forms feed it. `refuse_foreign_leases_held` reads the leases a held `claims_mutation_guard` read. `refuse_foreign_leases_read`, reached through the executor's `refuse_foreign_lease` and `refuse_foreign_leases`, reads them outside the claims lock and before the publishing session opens, with the mode taken from the executor's disk-backed configuration cache (`self.cached_config()`). The read form is called before publication by `assign_issue` and `unassign_issue` in the issue family, `add_gates`, `remove_gates`, `pass_gate` and `fail_gate` (`crates/jit/src/commands/gate.rs`), and by template application (`crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs`).
- `pass_gate` runs an automated gate's checker through `check_gate_with` (`crates/jit/src/commands/gate_check.rs`) after the lease check, so today a strict automated pass on another agent's lease is refused before the checker runs. `check_gate_with` captures its inputs in one session and records the run in a second; the checker runs between them, outside the lock. Upstream, the gate-capture and verdict-reuse changes rewrite this function: the inputs capture holds only the evaluated issue's named runs, and a reusable verdict is looked up from one verdict record, after the inputs session. The preliminary lease check is added to the inputs session as those changes leave it, ahead of both the reuse lookup and the checker. `gate evaluate-all` reaches the same path through `pass_all_gates`, which calls `pass_gate` per required gate.
- The in-session form already exists: the field update takes `claims_mutation_guard` before `open_mutation_session` and calls `refuse_foreign_leases_held` with the captured mode and issues (`publish_captured_field_update`). The guard is `None` outside a git repository, so an issue there has no lease to conflict (`@/charter/D-4`).
- The lifecycle path keeps a preliminary refusal: it refuses a claim on another agent's lease through a preliminary guard over the preflight image before running prechecks (`ensure_claim_available`), and repeats the check under the held guard when publishing. That refusal is part of the publishing operation and stays. The dedicated commands publish through `publish_captured_issue_mutation`.
- `apply_template_request` (`crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs`) opens a first session only to derive the lease targets and mode, computes warnings between sessions, then opens a second session, re-derives, and retries if the targets or mode changed; the claims guard is not held across publication. `DerivedTemplateApply::lease_targets` and `existing_template_lease_targets` already name the existing issues the apply edits.

title: Bulk update applies its matches in one session with no preview
description:
Delete the uncalled bulk-update preview and apply a bulk update in one publishing session: match over the captured issues, derive each matched issue's change against a projection that advances with each success, and publish one plan. The CLI reference describes the finished behaviour.

## Background

- `preview_bulk_update` (`crates/jit/src/commands/bulk_update.rs:458`) re-implements write validation with `compute_changes` (`:498`), `projected_after_update` (`:574`) and `validate_update_preview` (`:602`), and calls `transition_blockers` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:3258`, documented at `:3248` as serving the preview) once per matched issue, which lists every issue. It evaluates only local rules, from the executor's disk-backed cache, so it can disagree with apply. Nothing calls it: no reference exists in `main.rs`, `cli.rs`, the server, the MCP bridge, the web UI or the tests. Its result types `BulkUpdatePreview` and `PreviewSummary` (`bulk_update.rs:143-200`) are re-exported at `mod.rs:75` and used only by `test_preview_compute_summary` (`bulk_update.rs:729`); `compute_changes` has its own tests (`:745`, `:762`, `:784`).
- `apply_bulk_update` (`bulk_update.rs:234`, called from `crates/jit/src/main.rs:2623`) matches over an unlocked `list_issues` (`bulk_update.rs:243`), confirms provable no-ops in a shared verification session (`confirm_bulk_noop_candidates`, `bulk_update.rs:349`), then publishes each remaining issue in its own session through `apply_operations_to_issue` (`bulk_update.rs:445`) and `publish_captured_bulk_update` (`mod.rs:2686`), which calls `publish_captured_field_update` (`mod.rs:2599`). Each issue sees the earlier issues already published, so with B depending on A and both matched with `--state done`, A and then B reach Done.
- `QueryFilter::filter_issues` (`crates/jit/src/query_engine/mod.rs:53`) is pure, so matching can run over captured issues. `derive_field_update` (`mod.rs:1279`) is the per-issue derivation, and every field update carries its own readiness corrections.
- A `Ready` to `InProgress` change runs precheck gates whose checkers execute in a preflight session outside the repository lock, before the publishing session (the lifecycle pattern at `mod.rs:2790-2878`; the field path shares that state derivation). A batch whose matches include such a change needs that preflight once per attempt.
- A Done request with unpassed gates is diverted to Gated: the issue changes and the call also reports a `TransitionBlockedError` (`error_after_apply`), which bulk records in `errors`.
- The session-budget tests (`bulk_update.rs:1534-1995`) assert the per-issue session count and the shared verification session; `test_apply_bulk_update_terminal_state_promotes_unblocked_dependent_like_per_issue` and its neighbours (`:1998-2082`) assert readiness. Integration callers: `crates/jit/tests/fast_issue/transition_graph_enforcement_tests.rs` and `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/local_rule_enforcement_tests.rs`.
- `docs/reference/cli-commands.md:1026-1034` says bulk updates make no auto-transitions, publish one redo record per issue, and that only single-issue update enforces prechecks.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `preview_bulk_update`, `BulkUpdatePreview`, `PreviewSummary`, `compute_changes`, `projected_after_update`, `validate_update_preview` and `transition_blockers` no longer exist, nor does the re-export of `BulkUpdatePreview`; the tests that covered only those items are deleted and the remaining bulk-update tests pass unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-02: `apply_bulk_update` opens one publishing session per attempt, preceded by one precheck preflight session only when a matched change moves a `Ready` issue to `InProgress` with precheck gates; it matches over the publishing session's captured issues and publishes every non-rejected change, with its readiness corrections, in one redo record. `confirm_bulk_noop_candidates` and the per-issue publication path no longer exist.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each matched issue is derived against the projection left by the issues before it in match order; outcomes are reported as modified, skipped, failed, or diverted to Gated (modified and failed), as today, and a rejected issue does not stop the others from publishing.
- [hard] REQ-04: Harness tests show N matched issues needing change publishing one redo record (today N), and B depending on A with both matched by `--state done` ending with both Done.
- [hard] REQ-05: A harness test matches a `Ready` issue with a failing automatic precheck and another issue under `--state in_progress`: the first is reported in `errors` and stays `Ready`, the second moves, and the session counter shows one preflight and one publishing session.
- [hard] REQ-06: The bulk-update section of `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` states one-session, batch-atomic publication with readiness corrections, and its precheck statement covers both update paths (`issue update --state in_progress` and bulk transitions into `in_progress`).

## Notes

- Behaviour change: publication is batch-atomic, and a concurrent-write conflict retries the whole batch instead of one issue. A bulk transition into `InProgress` runs prechecks in a preflight before publication. The `apply_bulk_update` signature and `BulkUpdateResult` shape are unchanged.
- Behaviour is otherwise unchanged by the preview removal: no command or API exposed the preview.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

title: Bulk and dependency edits check leases in their publishing session
description:
Move the lease checks of bulk update and the CLI dependency edits into their publishing session, classify `dep add` and `dep rm` claims-first, and state in the adopter docs which writes the lease rule covers.

## Background

- Bulk update builds its requests with `enforce_lease: false` (`CapturedFieldUpdate::bulk`, `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs`) and checks its matched issues through `refuse_foreign_leases` before its session opens (`crates/jit/src/commands/bulk_update.rs`), outside the claims lock.
- `jit dep add` and `jit dep rm` publish the batch variants `CapturedDependencyMutation::Batch` and `RemoveBatch` (`crates/jit/src/commands/dependency.rs`), which check the dependent issue through `refuse_foreign_lease` before the session opens; only the single variants check inside the session under a claims guard. `DepCommands::coordinates_claims_first` (`crates/jit/src/cli.rs`) classifies both verbs repository-first; `CLAIM_FIRST_LEAF_COMMANDS` and its inventory test pin the classification.
- The in-session form is `refuse_foreign_leases_held` (`commands/mod.rs`) with a `claims_mutation_guard` taken before the session. A write refuses only when another agent holds an active lease on its target; an unleased issue has nothing to refuse (17fbcf25). Strict refusals downcast to `ForeignLeaseError` (`foreign-lease-error`).
- System-derived writes (readiness corrections of dependents, validate repairs, archive, recovery) are not user requests for the issues they touch.
- `docs/reference/configuration.md` and `docs/reference/claim.md` say lease enforcement covers "structural issue operations" and "selected write commands" without saying which.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Bulk update checks each matched issue it changes through `refuse_foreign_leases_held` inside its publishing session, holding the claims guard taken before it, and no longer calls the read form; in strict mode an issue under another agent's lease is reported in `errors` and the others still apply, and in warn mode the warning is reported for that issue.
- [hard] REQ-02: `dep add` and `dep rm` check the dependent issue's lease the same way inside their publishing session and no longer call the read form, and both are classified claims-first in the classification and its inventory test.
- [hard] REQ-03: Harness tests show strict mode refusing a bulk update and a `dep add` on another agent's lease with an error that downcasts to `ForeignLeaseError`, the same writes on an unleased issue succeeding, and no lease check for readiness corrections of dependents.
- [hard] REQ-04: The configuration and claim references state the lease-checked writes as a rule (every user-requested write to an existing issue refuses when another agent holds an active lease on an issue it targets, including bulk update, `dep add`/`dep rm`, assign, unassign, template application and the gate commands; system-derived writes check nothing) rather than a hand-kept command list, and no other page restates it (`@/charter/D-13`).

## Notes

- Behaviour change: bulk update and `dep add`/`dep rm` read leases under the claims lock, and the two dependency verbs lock claims before the repository; which writes refuse is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; locate symbols by name.

title: Every redo record appends an event, enforced by plan construction and storage
description:
Thread the operation's `MutationContext` into every materialization plan builder, make a plan that writes repository state without a domain event carry one generic `files_published` event naming the paths it writes, and make both storage backends refuse a record over a present data root that carries no event append, so the event log's length counts every commit and lock-free reads can rely on it (`@/charter/D-22`, `@/inv/event-log`).

## Background

- `MaterializationPlan::new(image, delta)` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mod.rs:624-633`) has seven production callers. Three builders already take a context: `finalize` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mutation.rs:715-723`), `finalize_gate_registry_edit` (`repository_state/mod.rs:78`, constructor at `:114`) and `finalize_archive_execution` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/archive.rs:22`, constructor at `:329`). Four take none: `derive_materialization` (`repository_state/mod.rs:713`, constructor at `:758`), `finalize_config_edit` (`:781`, constructor at `:814`), `finalize_package_tree_capture` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/package_tree.rs:229`, `:349`) and `finalize_repository_export` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/export.rs:154`, `:231`). `derive_materialization`'s initialize and profile-apply requests carry a context inside the request; its repair and projection-render requests carry none.
- Their callers: `derive_materialization` at `crates/jit/src/commands/init.rs:233,261`, `crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs:1440,1477`, `crates/jit/src/commands/project.rs:167`, `crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:634`, `crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:161,949` and the unit tests in `crates/jit/src/repository_state/materialize.rs`; `finalize_config_edit` at `crates/jit/src/commands/config.rs:278`; `finalize_package_tree_capture` at `profile.rs:625`; `finalize_repository_export` at `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2259,2285`. Of these, `validation/repository.rs:161` (the drift comparison inside `validate_repository`) and the unit tests derive plans that are never published; `validate.rs:634` sits in `capture_repair_plan` (`:603`), whose plan `jit validate --fix` and `jit recover` publish, and `project.rs:167` is `jit project render`'s published plan.
- `production_mutation_context` (`commands/mod.rs:137`) mints fresh ids and the current time. `MutationContext::preview` (`mutation.rs:276-281`) is deterministic: a zero seed and the Unix epoch, so every plan built with it gets the same ids and an epoch timestamp.
- `compose_event_action` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mutation.rs:1177-1240`) returns no append when there are no pending events (`:1182`) and otherwise takes each event's id and the timestamp from the context (`:1208-1213`); `redo_record_for` (`crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store.rs:1014-1044`) carries the append as optional (`:1035`). `jit config set` rewrites `.jit/config.toml` and leaves `events.jsonl` unchanged; project render, `validate --fix` repair, profile package trees and exports inside the repository are the other event-less publishers.
- `compose_event_action` owns event ordering, identity allocation and the mutation timestamp, and appends at the captured log's committed length, where an unterminated final line does not count. The event log changes only by a positioned append (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/image.rs`).
- Reports read `MaterializationPlan::delta()`: the drift classifier (`compare_materializations`, `repository_state/mod.rs:1036`; an append is `Stale` at `:1062`), the `validate --fix` messages (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:572-587`), and the preview reports.
- The append's expected preimage is the captured event-log entry; the config-set capture (`crates/jit/src/commands/config.rs:242-266`) captures only `config.toml` before growing to the validation closure. Neither `RepositoryExportIntent::capture_spec` (`export.rs:93-107`) nor `PackageTreeCapture::capture_spec` (`package_tree.rs:133-146`) captures `VirtualPath::EVENTS`.
- Event variants live in `crates/jit/src/domain/types.rs:1334`, their catalog in `crates/jit/src/domain/event_catalog.rs`, and `docs/reference/events.md` is generated by `scripts/generate-events-reference.sh`.
- `JsonMutationSession::publish_through_record` (`repository_state_store.rs:619-633`) and `MemoryMutationSession::publish_through_record` (`:770-784`) build the record with `redo_record_for` and commit it; `RedoRecord::event_append` (`crates/jit/src/storage/redo_record.rs:110`) is optional. The absent-root path (`publish_absent_data_root`, `repository_state_store.rs:643-701`) commits a worktree-only record inside the new root and is exempt: a reader observes that root's appearance.
- The memory backend's record commit is `InMemoryStorage::commit_record` (`crates/jit/src/storage/memory.rs:499`). Shared session contract tests over both backends live in `crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store_tests.rs`.
- `docs/reference/storage-format.md:96-100` says a read-only command opens no mutation session and reads files as they stand, which may be a partly applied state.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `MaterializationPlan::new` takes `&MutationContext` and every builder that constructs a plan takes one. Every caller whose plan is published (derived-state repair, project render, config set, export, package tree, init and profile apply) passes `production_mutation_context()` or the production context its operation already holds; only derivations that are never published, such as the drift comparison in `validate_repository` and unit tests, pass `MutationContext::preview()`. No plan's delta, projection counts or profile records change: the existing materialization, export, package-tree, archive and configuration tests pass unchanged apart from the added argument.
- [hard] REQ-02: A `files_published` event carrying the sorted repository-relative paths a plan writes, makes or deletes is declared in the event catalog and `docs/reference/events.md` is regenerated. `MaterializationPlan::new` keeps the derived delta as `delta()` and exposes `publication()`: the derived delta plus one `files_published` append, composed through `compose_event_action`, when the delta writes over a present data root and carries no append; otherwise the derived delta. Both backends' `apply` publish `publication()`, and reports keep reading `delta()`.
- [hard] REQ-03: Every publishing capture whose delta can lack a domain event includes the event-log tail, `RepositoryExportIntent::capture_spec` and `PackageTreeCapture::capture_spec` included; constructing a plan that needs the generic event over an image without it fails with a typed error that a unit test covers.
- [hard] REQ-04: Both `publish_through_record` implementations refuse a record with no event append, with one typed `RepositoryStateStoreError` variant, before the record is committed; the absent-root publication is unchanged. A contract test run against both backends applies a plan whose publication writes a file and appends nothing and asserts the typed refusal, an unchanged repository and no record left behind.
- [hard] REQ-05: A CLI test in `crates/jit/tests/cli_item_validate/project_render_cli_tests.rs` runs `jit config set` and `jit project render` with a changed projection and finds the event log grown by one `files_published` event naming the written paths; the two events carry distinct ids and timestamps after the epoch; a no-op of either appends nothing.
- [hard] REQ-06: `docs/reference/storage-format.md` states that every redo record appends an event, including `files_published` for event-less writes.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: each event-less write appends one `files_published` event at the log's committed length, as event-bearing writes do. The drift report and the `validate --fix` messages are unchanged because they read `delta()`.
- Behaviour change: storage refuses, before commit, a publication over a present data root whose redo record carries no event append; production plans all carry an append after the `files_published` step, so their behaviour is unchanged.
- The context threading is a step inside this task; `finalize_archive_execution` already holds a context, so its edit is the constructor call only.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

title: Lock-free read session with commit admission and one read driver
description:
Split the capture half of the mutation session into a `RepositoryReadSession` trait, add a lock-free read session to both backends admitted only when no redo record was present and the event log did not grow across its capture, and add the one driver every read uses: bounded optimistic attempts, then one attempt in the operation's mutation session that completes a leftover redo record (`optimistic-read-admission`, `read-session-driver`, `@/charter/D-20`, `@/charter/D-22`).

## Background

- `RepositoryMutationSession` (`crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store.rs:213-232`) declares `layout`, `recovery_report`, `capture`, `extend` and `apply`; `RepositoryStateStore` (`:235-242`) opens it. Both are re-exported at `crates/jit/src/storage/mod.rs:84-87`.
- Implementors outside the session module: `RoundCounter` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:3411`), and two probe pairs in integration tests, `PublicationProbeSession`/`PublicationProbeStore` (`crates/jit/tests/fast_docs_templates/template_apply_atomicity_tests.rs:216`, `:301`) and `FailingMutationSession`/`FailingMutationStorage` (`crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/local_rule_enforcement_tests.rs:797`, `:833`).
- Shared capture helpers take `&mut dyn RepositoryMutationSession` although they never apply: `capture_discovering` and `grow_discovering` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:339`, `:354`), and in `crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs` `capture_proposed_base` (`:182`), `capture_archive_base` (`:305`), `capture_proposed_base_inner` (`:331`) and `capture_repair_plan` (`:603`). `capture_mutation_base` (`:211`) serves only publishing callers.
- The workspace MSRV is 1.97 (`Cargo.toml:11`), so a `&mut dyn RepositoryMutationSession` coerces implicitly to a supertrait object, and existing call sites compile unchanged.
- `JsonFileStorage::open_mutation_session` (`repository_state_store.rs:424-510`) enters the layout-reentry and order guards (`:453-457`), takes the worktree bootstrap lock (`:466-467`) and the bootstrap lock (`:472`), opens `CapabilityRoots` (`:475`), reads the leftover record (`read_leftover_record`, `:269-294`), crosses `MutationPoint::SessionOpen` (`:477`), then takes the repository write lock and the events lock (`:480-481`) and applies the record. The memory backend's open (`:513-542`) takes its in-process lock, crosses `SessionOpen` (`:522`) and reads `state.record` (`crates/jit/src/storage/memory.rs:63`). `MutationPoint` is declared in `crates/jit/src/storage/mutation_interruption.rs:12-25`.
- Capture is lock-free code already: `capture_capability_image` (`repository_state_store.rs:1112`) and `capture_memory_image` (`:1227`); the session wrappers are `capture_over` (`:605`, `:756`). `revalidate_layout_capabilities` (`:1913-1930`) returns `RetryableConflict` when a root was replaced or the data root's presence changed, and `live_event_log_tail` (`:1079`) reads the log's length and tail window as `EventLogTail`.
- A redo record is committed before its first live write (`RedoRecord::commit`, `crates/jit/src/storage/redo_record.rs:208-217`). Application makes directories, puts, deletes, then writes the event append (`crates/jit/src/storage/redo_apply.rs:130-175`), and `RedoApplier::apply` (`:117-127`) removes the record before it crosses `RedoPoint::AfterApply`. The memory backend commits in one state section (`commit_record`, `memory.rs:499`) and applies, appends and clears `state.record` (`:580`) in another (`MemoryRedoApplier::apply`, `:533-582`), also before `AfterApply`.
- The soundness argument and the rejected alternatives are in `dev/active/b697a3f7-one-mutation-path/investigation-read-concurrency.md` §2.
- `with_mutation_session` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:455`) opens a mutation session per attempt over `with_mutation_attempts` (`:412`) with `MUTATION_SESSION_RETRY_LIMIT = 8` (`:264`); `SessionStep` (`:438`) carries `Done`, `Retry` and `Apply`. `capture_or_retry` (`:320`) folds a retryable capture conflict into `None`.
- A torn image can make a derivation fail (for example on a dangling reference), so an attempt's error is meaningful only after admission.
- A leftover-record failure is classified by `is_leftover_record_failure` (`repository_state_store.rs:89`). `open_repository` wraps it in `RecoveryFailedError` (`crates/jit/src/commands/bootstrap.rs:45`, wrapped at `:115-116`) only for `jit recover`, and `main.rs` unwraps that type (`crates/jit/src/main.rs:1650-1655`) into `exit_recovery_failed` (`:173`), which renders `ErrorCode::RecoveryFailed` (`crates/jit/src/output.rs:1060`). `classify_code` (`crates/jit/src/output/failure.rs:20`) maps nothing to `RecoveryFailed`.
- Contention tests over a shared store live in `crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store_contention_tests.rs`; session contract tests live in `crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store_tests.rs`.

## Success Criteria

title: Validate, link checks and profile previews read through the read driver
description:
Move `jit validate` without `--fix`, `--fix --dry-run`, the other readers of the validation capture, `jit doc check-links`, profile planning, profile difference reports and the `profile add` and `profile pack` dry runs onto `with_read_session`, each over the same capture-and-derive function its publishing operation runs, so these reads run beside writers, and state the read discipline in `docs/reference/storage-format.md` (`@/charter/D-20`, `@/charter/D-22`).

## Background

Before 1f24e3e9 lands, `--fix --dry-run` reaches `repair_derived_state(true)` (`:72`, `:552-600`). After it, `repair_derived_state` (deriving through `capture_repair_plan`, `:603`) is called only by `jit recover` (`execute_recover`, `crates/jit/src/commands/claim.rs:725`), which publishes. `validate --fix --dry-run` is not recovery-dispatched (`crates/jit/src/cli.rs:2675`).

The CLI arm is `crates/jit/src/main.rs:5065-5072`; CLI tests are in `crates/jit/tests/cli_query_graph/check_links_tests.rs`.
- `plan_profile_package_with_inputs` (`crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs:811-845`) and `preview_resolved_profile_selection` (`:1275-1313`, serving `plan_profiles` through `plan_resolved_profile_selection` at `:1252`, and `diff_profiles_from_sources` at `:963`) open `with_mutation_session` and return `SessionStep::Done` over `prepare_profile_selection` (`:1362`), which takes `&mut dyn RepositoryMutationSession` and calls `capture_proposed_base`.

Dry runs are not recovery-dispatched (`crates/jit/src/cli.rs:2744`).

A read-session open crosses `MutationPoint::ReadSessionOpen`, not `SessionOpen`; command tests race a writer at a session point through `with_session_race` (`crates/jit/src/commands/test_helpers.rs:132`).
- `test_package_tree_publication_has_one_owner_in_the_command_layer` (`crates/jit/tests/scratch_build/repository_state_cutover_tests.rs:1531-1548`) requires `commands/profile.rs` to contain exactly one `finalize_package_tree_capture(` call, exactly one `PackageTreeCapture::new(` call, and `fn publish_package_tree(`.

title: Cost evidence: the epic's four cost reductions against the base binary
description:
Build one harness that measures the four cost claims of this epic against a pinned pre-change binary and any tip binary, with ratio thresholds computed within one run, record that the base reproduces each cost, and record the tip run once the four reductions have landed (`@/charter/D-17`, `@/charter/D-19`).

title: One pure assembler builds every JitConfig from source bytes
description:
Add one public pure function that assembles a `JitConfig` from the bytes of `config.toml`, `templates.toml` and `invariants.toml`, route every configuration assembly through it, and remove the `ConfigurationDeclarations` mirror of `JitConfig` fields, so configuration has one set of assembly rules and captured declarations carry the assembled configuration once.

## Background

- Three paths assemble a `JitConfig` today, each with different rules:
  - `JitConfig::load` (`crates/jit/src/config.rs:1361-1430`) reads `config.toml`, loads `templates.toml` with node types checked against `[type_hierarchy].types` (`:1407-1413`; `TemplateRegistry::load` at `:1381`, `:1412`), runs `JitConfig::validate_item_kinds` (`config.rs:1444`, at `:1419-1421`) and loads `invariants.toml` (`:1387`, `:1426-1427`). An absent `config.toml` yields the empty configuration with templates and invariants still loaded (`:1364-1389`).
  - `assemble_config` and `assemble_config_from_declarations` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/materialize.rs:67-93`) require a captured `config.toml` (`ProducerError::MissingCapture` when captured absent) and add only the invariant registry: no templates, no item-kind validation.
  - `declarations_from_image` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mod.rs:411-419`) and `validation_declarations_from_image` (`mod.rs:425`) parse the config with `parse_configuration` and reassemble it through `assemble_config_from_declarations` (`:431-432`); the validation variant layers templates (`:444-453`) but skips item-kind validation.
- The pure parts exist: `crate::declarations::parse_configuration` (`crates/jit/src/declarations/mod.rs:65-78`), `TemplateRegistry::from_toml_str` (`crates/jit/src/templates.rs:451`), `InvariantRegistry::from_toml_str` (`crates/jit/src/declarations/invariants.rs:162`), `JitConfig::validate_item_kinds`, and the default accessors `JitConfig::content_format()`/`strictness()` (`config.rs:1339,1350`). `config.toml` decoding is strict about unknown keys.
- Because no capture validates `[item_kinds]`, repository validation checks it at report time (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:192-200`) and fails the whole validation run there.
- Sites that still compose a `JitConfig` or parse `config.toml` themselves:
  - `effective_config` and `empty_materialization_config` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:700-723`) parse overlaid config bytes and add invariants; callers `capture_proposed_base_inner` (`validate.rs:403-404`) and `plan_content_with_issues` (`validate.rs:970`).
  - `template_config_from_image` (`crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs:547-571`) treats an absent config as `toml::from_str("")` and layers templates itself (`:565`); `template_declarations_from_image` (`template.rs:574-611`) builds its own rule set and a placeholder `parse_configuration(b"")` (`:603`).
  - `InitializationRequest::from_config` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/initialize.rs:213-243`) parses the generated config and calls `materialization_config` with an empty invariant registry (`:218-220`).
  - `finalize_config_edit` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mod.rs:781`) parses the edited `config.toml` with `parse_configuration` (`:788`) before planning.
  - `configured_projection_targets` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/profile_apply.rs:1331-1348`) parses captured config bytes for projection targets (`:1344`).
  - `resolve_init_config` (`crates/jit/src/commands/init.rs:341`) reads the project name through `parse_configuration` (`:366`).
  - `config set` validates the edited document through `parse_configuration` in `edit_config_document` (`crates/jit/src/commands/config.rs:191`).
- `ConfigurationDeclarations` (`crates/jit/src/declarations/mod.rs:30-62`) keeps a parsed `JitConfig` plus cloned copies of its `hierarchy`, `namespaces`, `item_kinds`, `projections` and `documentation` fields; `materialization_config` (`:54`) clones the parse again. `parse_configuration` (`:65-78`) builds it.
- `RepositoryDeclarations` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mod.rs:342`) lends `&ConfigurationDeclarations` (`:344`), and `CapturedRepositoryDeclarations` (`mod.rs:353`) stores it (`:354`) beside `config` (`:355`; `from_parts` `:362-364`). Producers re-derive the config from it with `assemble_config_from_declarations` in `compose_complete` (`mod.rs:883`), `derive_project_render` (`:914`) and `repair_target_paths` (`:972`).
- Remaining readers of the mirror once every production site assembles through the assembler: `CapturedRepositoryDeclarations::from_parts` in `crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs:602-603`; the test fixtures `empty_declarations` (`repository_state/mod.rs:1299-1301`), `declarations` and `config_decls` (`materialize.rs:884-929`); `crates/jit/src/commands/init.rs` tests (`:1126`, `:1322`); `crates/jit/tests/cli_repo_workflow/init_tests.rs` (`:4`, `:71`, `:689`); and `test_load_rejects_unknown_key_by_name_in_every_table` (`crates/jit/src/config.rs:2073`, calling `parse_configuration` at `:2095`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A `pub` function in `crate::declarations` takes optional `config.toml`, `templates.toml` and `invariants.toml` bytes and returns a `JitConfig` or a typed error naming the failing source: an absent config yields the empty configuration, templates are parsed against the declared hierarchy types, `[item_kinds]` is validated, and absent templates or invariants yield empty registries. Unit tests cover an absent config, absent templates and invariants, a template node type outside the declared hierarchy, a malformed `[item_kinds]` table and an unknown `config.toml` key.
- [hard] REQ-02: `JitConfig::load`, `assemble_config`, `declarations_from_image`, `validation_declarations_from_image` and every site listed in Background obtain their `JitConfig` through the assembler; outside the assembler and test code, nothing parses `config.toml` into a configuration, deserializes `JitConfig` from TOML, or populates its template or invariant registry, and `validate_repository_with_materializations` no longer re-validates `[item_kinds]`. `template_declarations_from_image` builds its rule set through the captured-declaration parse the other mutation paths use.
- [hard] REQ-03: Capturing declarations from an image whose `config.toml` declares a malformed `[item_kinds]` table fails with the assembler's item-kind error, and assembling an image that captured `config.toml` as absent yields the empty configuration, as disk loading does. Both tests fail today (`validation_declarations_from_image` returns the declarations successfully; `assemble_config` fails on `ProducerError::MissingCapture`).
- [hard] REQ-04: A `config set` or config edit whose result fails assembly, such as a malformed `[item_kinds]` table, is refused when planned, asserted by one test that fails today.
- [hard] REQ-05: `ConfigurationDeclarations`, `parse_configuration`, `materialization_config` and `assemble_config_from_declarations` no longer exist; captured and lent declaration bundles carry the assembled `JitConfig` as their only configuration, and producers that received declarations read the configuration from the bundle without reassembling it from the image.

title: Storage reads configuration files and the registry file loaders are gone
description:
Add a storage module that reads the configuration files and returns the assembled configuration, move every caller and integration test that loads configuration from disk onto it, and delete the template and invariant registry file loaders, so file reads for declarations live in the storage layer and the declaration modules only parse bytes.

## Background

- The configuration files are read outside storage: `JitConfig::load` (`crates/jit/src/config.rs:1361-1430`) reads a directory's `config.toml`, `templates.toml` and `invariants.toml`. `EffectiveConfig::load` (`config.rs:1503-1507`) calls it on the repository data root, the only configuration layer; `config validate` calls it on the same data root (`crates/jit/src/main.rs:5609-5615`). Its rustdoc (`config.rs:1501-1502`) and `effective_config_snapshot`'s (`crates/jit/src/commands/config.rs:294-295`) claim config I/O lives in the config layer.
- The storage precedent is `load_ruleset` (`crates/jit/src/storage/ruleset_store.rs:19`), which reads `rules.toml` and the schema files for a data root.
- Configuration is assembled from bytes by the public assembler in `crate::declarations` (`configuration-assembly`); repository file names come from the `VirtualPath` constants.
- Callers:
  - `effective_config_snapshot` (`crates/jit/src/commands/config.rs:296-298`) and the dotted-key lookup beside it call `EffectiveConfig::load`;
  - claim acquisition calls `JitConfig::load(&paths.local_jit)?.coordination()` for policy limits (`crates/jit/src/commands/claim.rs:108-109`);
  - `config validate` probes the repository `config.toml` and calls `JitConfig::load` (`crates/jit/src/main.rs:5609-5615`);
  - the taxonomy fixture test calls `JitConfig::load` (`crates/jit/src/test_utils.rs:2271`).
- Five integration test files call `JitConfig::load` on a temporary `.jit` directory: `crates/jit/tests/cli_item_validate/invariant_registry_story_tests.rs` (12 calls), `crates/jit/tests/fast_docs_templates/templates_loader_tests.rs` (7), `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/config_loading_tests.rs` (3: `:47`, `:71`, `:133`), `crates/jit/tests/cli_repo_workflow/project_config_tests.rs` (`:89`) and `crates/jit/tests/fast_docs_templates/archive_path_layout_tests.rs` (`:86`).
- `crate::declarations` is documented as filesystem-free (`crates/jit/src/declarations/mod.rs:1`), yet `InvariantRegistry::load` (`crates/jit/src/declarations/invariants.rs:144-160`) reads `invariants.toml` and `TemplateRegistry::load` (`crates/jit/src/templates.rs:432-450`) reads `templates.toml`. Once `JitConfig::load` assembles through the assembler (`configuration-assembly`) neither has a production caller. Their remaining test callers: `invariants.rs` `test_load_absent_file_is_empty_registry` (`:310`), `test_load_reads_present_file` (`:317`), `test_load_malformed_file_is_typed_error` (`:331`); `templates.rs` `test_load_missing_file_is_empty_registry` (`:808`), `test_load_valid_file_from_disk` (`:815`), `test_malformed_toml_errors` (`:824`), `test_repo_plan_template_parses` (`:1114`); and `test_config_load_succeeds_with_valid_templates` (`crates/jit/tests/fast_docs_templates/templates_loader_tests.rs:64`, load at `:70`). Both registries keep `from_toml_str` (`templates.rs:451`, `invariants.rs:162`), whose tests own parsing.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `crates/jit/src/storage/configuration_store.rs` reads a data root's `config.toml`, `templates.toml` and `invariants.toml` and returns the assembler's result; it is exported from `crate::storage`. - [hard] REQ-02: `EffectiveConfig` in `config.rs` is built from an already-loaded repository configuration and performs no filesystem I/O; the read happens in the storage loader. The callers in `commands/config.rs`, `commands/claim.rs`, `main.rs` and `test_utils.rs` load configuration through the storage loader, and `config show`, `config get`, `config validate` and claim acquisition report the same values and errors as before; their existing suites pass unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: None of the five integration test files calls `JitConfig::load`; each loads through the storage loader, every test keeps its assertions, and each file passes alone and in parallel.
- [hard] REQ-04: `TemplateRegistry::load` and `InvariantRegistry::load` no longer exist and neither `crates/jit/src/templates.rs` nor `crates/jit/src/declarations/invariants.rs` touches the filesystem. The registry-loader tests listed in Background are deleted where they only re-prove the absent-file or malformed-file mapping the assembler's tests own, or are rewritten over `from_toml_str`; no parsing case is lost.

title: Read paths take declarations from one captured-declaration helper
description:
Give read paths one public executor helper that captures the repository's declaration files through the read driver and returns them parsed, with the label namespaces and the type hierarchy derived from them, and move the command, CLI and server configuration reads onto it, so reads take no declarations from disk or the executor caches.

## Background

- Read commands take configuration from disk: the executor's `OnceLock` caches (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2120-2182`) and `crate::config_manager::get_hierarchy_config` (`crates/jit/src/config_manager.rs:263-275`). Write paths read the same declarations from a captured image through `declarations_from_image` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mod.rs:411-420`).
- Reads run through `with_read_session` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs`, next to `with_mutation_session` at `:455`), whose closure takes `&mut dyn RepositoryReadSession`. The repository layout names its declaration files through one layout-level set.
- `validation_declarations_from_image` (`repository_state/mod.rs:425`) computes the namespace registry (`:454`) and discards it. The type hierarchy is built from that registry through `HierarchyConfig::from_declarations`.
- `CapturedRepositoryDeclarations` and its accessors are `pub(crate)` (`repository_state/mod.rs:353-407`). The server crate and the integration tests cannot name a crate-private type, and a `pub` method returning it fails the `private_interfaces` lint.
- Rule schemas are named inside `rules.toml`, so the capture needs a second discovery round for them, as the validation base capture does (`capture_proposed_base_inner`, `validate.rs:331`, schema discovery at `:410`).
- `linked_checkout_write_decision` (`crates/jit/src/commands/bootstrap.rs:218-244`) reads the declared stance with `ConfigManager::new(jit_dir).get_write_policy()` (`:227`). `open_repository` calls it at `:88`, before the storage handle exists (`:95`) and the executor is built (`:125`); the comments at `:67-69` and `:86-87` state the contract that a refusal precedes every lock and write. Its tests are at `bootstrap.rs:392-509`, with fixtures from `:365`.
- In `crates/jit/src/main.rs`, `label namespaces` (`:5469-5471`) and `config show-hierarchy` (`:5668-5670`) read namespaces through `ConfigManager::get_namespaces`.
- `crates/server/src/routes.rs`: `get_graph` calls `get_hierarchy_config` (`:188`); `get_strategic_types`, `get_hierarchy` and `get_namespaces` call `config_manager.get_namespaces()` (`:942-943, 968-969, 1013-1014`, in handlers at `:937`, `:963`, `:1008`), and `get_hierarchy` calls `get_hierarchy_icons()` (`:981-982`). The server holds one long-lived executor, so a stale disk read there persists.
- `AppState` (`routes.rs:28`), `create_routes` (`:38`) and the handlers are bound only by `S: IssueStore`; capture needs `S: RepositoryStateStore` as well (one handler at `:1066` already carries both). The document handlers (`:295, 603-612, 633-642, 797-803, 842-851`) reach `with_issue_documents`. The server binary (`crates/server/src/main.rs:104`) and the document API tests (`crates/server/tests/server_integration/document_api_tests.rs:28,59`) build `AppState` over concrete stores that implement both traits.
- Icon resolution is a pure computation over `[type_hierarchy]` inside `ConfigManager::get_hierarchy_icons` (`crates/jit/src/config_manager.rs:175-195`). The storage configuration loader (`crates/jit/src/storage/configuration_store.rs`, from `configuration-store`) reads `config.toml` through storage without opening a session or taking a lock.
- Command read paths that read configuration from disk or the executor caches:
  - `crates/jit/src/commands/graph.rs`: `export_graph` (`:235`), `export_graph_batch` (`:316`), `identity_bound_namespaces` (`:404,409`), `bracket_node_types` (`:431`), `resolve_hierarchy_tree` (`:497`), `detect_divergences` (`:584`).
  - `crates/jit/src/commands/item.rs`: `item_kinds` (`:72-73`), `list_items` (`:135`), `project_items` (`:287`), `show_item` (`:365`), `resolve_item_address` (`:479-481`, reads the project name through `self.config_manager.project_name_from_config(self.cached_config()?)`). The test comment at `:1532` names `cached_config`.
  - `crates/jit/src/commands/document.rs`: `with_issue_documents` (`:160-165`, `config_manager.load()` plus `get_hierarchy_config`), `resolve_issue_artifact_directory` (`:284-289`), `report_artifact_conformance` (`:340-345`).
  - `query_strategic` (`crates/jit/src/commands/query.rs:57-58`) reads namespaces through `ConfigManager::get_namespaces`. `CommandExecutor::container_anchor` (`crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs:98-100`) also reads the cached config, but no production code calls it: `jit apply` binds the anchor from the captured config in `captured_anchor_bindings` (`template.rs:250`, binding at `:259`). `executor-config-caches-removal` deletes it.
- The helper requires `S: RepositoryStateStore`. Every document reader that reaches `with_issue_documents` therefore gains the bound: the server-called `read_document_content` (`document.rs:667`), `read_document_bytes` (`:701`), `get_document_history` (`:732`), `get_document_diff` (`:765`) and `get_issue_document_paths` (`:822`), whose handlers already carry it; and the CLI-only `list_document_references` (`:237`), `show_document_content` (`:498`), `document_history` (`:557`) and `document_diff` (`:582`). `check_document_links` (`:1098`) already carries it. `dangling_link_findings` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:1242`), which calls `item_kinds()` under `S: IssueStore` alone, is deleted upstream with the executor-side validation passes.
- Harness tests that seed configuration for an in-memory executor must seed it into storage, as `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/label_strategic_tests.rs:21-22` and `crates/jit/tests/fast_docs_templates/template_binding_tests.rs:109-110` already do, because a memory-backed capture sees only stored bytes.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One `pub` executor method captures the layout's declaration files, and the rule schemas `rules.toml` names, in one `with_read_session` closure and returns them parsed once through the captured-declaration parse. `CapturedRepositoryDeclarations` is `pub`, with `pub` accessors for the configuration, rules, gates, the label namespace registry and a fallible `hierarchy()` computed from the declarations without any disk read. A harness test over in-memory storage shows that the helper returns the same configuration, rules and namespaces as parsing the captured image directly, and that the store holds the same bytes before and after the call.
- [hard] REQ-02: The server's hierarchy, strategic-type and namespace routes and the CLI's `label namespaces` and `config show-hierarchy` arms obtain namespaces, hierarchy and icons from the helper, with hierarchy icons coming from one pure function over a `JitConfig`; none calls a `ConfigManager` reader or `get_hierarchy_config`. `AppState`, `create_routes` and every handler require `S: IssueStore + RepositoryStateStore`, and the server binary and its tests compile with the stores they use.
- [hard] REQ-03: `linked_checkout_write_decision` reads the declared stance through the storage configuration loader with no session and no lock, and its existing refusal and override tests pass unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-04: The graph, item, document and strategic-query functions listed in Background take hierarchy, namespaces, item kinds, templates, rules and the project name from the helper; none calls `get_hierarchy_config`, a `ConfigManager` reader or the executor's configuration and rule caches (`container_anchor` excepted: `executor-config-caches-removal` deletes it).
- [hard] REQ-05: Every function on these read paths that now captures, the document readers named in Background included, declares `S: RepositoryStateStore`, the workspace, the server included, compiles, and the graph, item, document, batch-export and strategic-query suites pass, with harness fixtures seeding configuration into storage where they relied on disk.
- [hard] REQ-06: `docs/reference/storage-format.md` lists the declaration reads (the graph, item, document and strategic-query commands, `label namespaces`, `config show-hierarchy` and the server's configuration routes) among the commands that read through the driver, under the rule `lock-free-read-consumers` states.

## Notes

- Behaviour changes: reads that use the helper take no repository lock while uncontended and complete a leftover redo record only through the driver's locked fallback (`@/charter/D-22`).
- The linked-checkout decision is the stated exception to captured reads: it must refuse before any lock or session exists, so it reads one file through storage.
- `item_kinds` and the content-format reads in `list_items`, `project_items` and `show_item` are edited by the configuration-default accessor change upstream; this task takes them as that change leaves them.
- `lock-free-read-consumers`, which this task follows, owns the read-discipline statement in `docs/reference/storage-format.md`; this task adds only its own commands to the list there.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

title: The executor holds no disk-backed configuration; ConfigManager and JitConfig::load are gone
description:
Remove the executor's disk-backed configuration, namespace and rule caches, move their last readers and tests onto captured declarations, delete `get_hierarchy_config` and `ConfigManager`, keeping its pure conversions as free functions, and delete `JitConfig::load`, so no command reads declarations from a per-process cache that can disagree with the captured image, and `config.rs` and the declaration modules only parse and merge.

## Background

- `CommandExecutor` holds `rules`, `effective_rules`, `config` and `namespaces` as `OnceLock`s (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2129-2149`, initialised at `:2180-2183`), filled by `rules()` (`:2480-2492`, which calls `crate::storage::ruleset_store::load_ruleset` on the live root through `config_manager`), `effective_rules()` (`:2523-2553`, which probes `rules.toml` on disk and reconciles default rules with the namespace registry), `cached_config()` (`:2560-2568`, `config_manager.load()`), `cached_namespaces()` (`:2574-2592`) and `repo_content_format()` (`:2595`). `worktree_paths` (`:2170`) is an injected authority, not configuration, and stays.
- After the read paths, bulk preview, lease check and executor-side validation views have moved off them, no production reader remains. `CommandExecutor::container_anchor` (`crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs:98-100`) reads `self.cached_config()?.templates.anchors`, but only tests call it (`crates/jit/tests/fast_docs_templates/template_binding_tests.rs:161, 219, 247`); `jit apply` binds the anchor from the captured config in `captured_anchor_bindings` (`template.rs:250`, binding at `:259`). `cached_namespaces` keeps readers only inside `effective_rules` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2537, 2547`). The remaining test readers are the cache-owning unit tests (`test_rules_are_parsed_once_and_cached` `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:4088`, `test_namespaces_are_parsed_once_and_cached` `:4142`, `test_rules_missing_file_yields_empty_ok` `:4192`, `test_rules_malformed_file_yields_err` `:4205`) and a `cached_config()` read in `test_effective_configuration_loads_an_authored_edit_of_a_published_registry` (`crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs:3645`, reading at `:3667`).
- Tests that call `effective_rules` directly: `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/default_rules_registry_derivation_tests.rs` (`:106, 184, 225, 254, 293`): default rules re-derive from the declared registry; `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/effective_rules_tests.rs` (`:57, 71, 86`, module doc `:1-9`): present, empty and absent `rules.toml`; `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/project_render_harness_tests.rs:217`: primes the stale cache to show render ignores it. The captured parse (`validation_declarations_from_image`, `crates/jit/src/repository_state/mod.rs:425`) implements the same present, empty, absent and reconciliation semantics, and the public captured-declaration helper exposes its rules.
- Outside storage, `load_ruleset` (`crates/jit/src/storage/ruleset_store.rs:19`) has no other production caller than `rules()`; the remaining callers are tests and doc examples (`crates/jit/src/validation/engine.rs`, `validation/local.rs`, `repository_state/rule_serialize.rs`, `profile/repository_package.rs`). The properties the cache-owning tests own besides caching (absent rules file yields an empty set, a malformed one an error) are owned by the rule-set loader and the captured parse.
- `crate::config_manager::get_hierarchy_config` (`crates/jit/src/config_manager.rs:263-275`) re-reads `config.toml`, `templates.toml` and `invariants.toml` on every call. `ConfigManager` (`crates/jit/src/config_manager.rs:28-196`) holds only a root path: `load` (`config_manager.rs:48`), `get_namespaces` (`config_manager.rs:60`), `get_write_policy` (`config_manager.rs:89`), `get_project_name` (`config_manager.rs:151`) and `get_hierarchy_icons` (`config_manager.rs:175`) read the same files, and `namespaces_from_config` (`config_manager.rs:71`), `write_policy_from_config` (`config_manager.rs:96`), `invocation_write_override` (`config_manager.rs:125`) and `project_name_from_config` (`config_manager.rs:162`) are pure conversions written as methods.

title: Mutation bases carry their parsed declarations and derivations reuse them
description:
Give the captured mutation base one memoised parse of its image's declarations and make the mutation derivations reuse it, so a mutation parses each captured image's configuration, gates and rules at most once.

## Background

- `MutationBase` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:863-868`) holds only the captured image and its issues, and `capture_mutation_base` (`validate.rs:211-227`) returns it. Every consumer that needs configuration, gates or rules parses the image again through `declarations_from_image` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mod.rs:411`) or `assemble_config` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/materialize.rs:67`).
