title: One pure gate-preset catalog serves every preset reader
description:
Add one public, pure gate-preset catalog built from a captured image, move every preset reader onto it, and delete `PresetManager` and the `IssueStore` preset methods, so presets are listed, parsed and looked up in one place with no preset file I/O outside storage capture.

## Background

- `load_presets_from_custom_files` (`crates/jit/src/gate_presets.rs:158`, `pub(crate)`) is the shared parse policy: canonical names, `.json` suffix, filename stem equal to the embedded name, sorted diagnostics. `PresetInfo` is declared at `gate_presets.rs:189`; `gate_presets` is a public module (`crates/jit/src/lib.rs:17`).
- Two command-layer image readers wrap that policy with their own listing helpers today: `listed_gate_preset_paths` and `parse_captured_gate_presets` (`crates/jit/src/commands/gate.rs:244,262`), and `listed_json_paths` and `parse_template_presets` (`crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs:620,690`). Both filter `*.json` names of the `VirtualPath::GATE_PRESETS` listing (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/path.rs:342`). `capture_gate_preset_image` (`gate.rs:292`) uses the listing helper to extend its capture (`:330`), and `apply_gate_preset` (`:1256`) looks the preset up through `parse_captured_gate_presets` (`:1305`). The template capture uses its listing helper (`template.rs:401`), and `derive_captured_template_apply` (`:330`) parses the presets at `:342`.
- `CommandExecutor::list_gate_presets` and `show_gate_preset` (`gate.rs:1242-1251`) forward to `IssueStore::list_gate_presets` and `get_gate_preset` (`crates/jit/src/storage/mod.rs:356,363`). The JSON backend reads the presets directory from disk through `PresetManager` (`crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:1445-1453`); the memory backend parses its own state (`crates/jit/src/storage/memory.rs:901-921`, over the helper `gate_presets_from_repository_state`, `memory.rs:204-240`). `gate preset apply` reads the captured image instead (`apply_gate_preset`, `gate.rs:1256-1311`), so show and apply read two sources. `main.rs` calls both methods (`crates/jit/src/main.rs:4194,4236`); their signatures stay. Reads run through `with_read_session` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs`), whose closure takes `&mut dyn RepositoryReadSession`.
- `PresetManager` (`crates/jit/src/gate_presets/manager.rs:10-97`, a 342-line file) reads `.jit/config/gate-presets/` with `fs::read_dir` (`load_presets`, `manager.rs:24-64`, read at `:43`) and a nix no-follow open on a path joined from literals (`read_regular_preset_no_follow`, `:100-148`). It is re-exported at `crates/jit/src/gate_presets.rs:18`, named in that module's rustdoc (`:8-12`, which also says every preset is a project's own; no built-in presets exist), and used only by the JSON backend and its own tests. Its tests own properties a captured reader must keep: a missing presets directory lists nothing, a symlinked or non-file `*.json` occupant is refused, invalid JSON and a stem mismatch are refused, and the listing is sorted by name (`manager.rs:178-341`).
- `IssueStore::list_gate_presets` and `get_gate_preset` are also forwarded by two test wrappers (`crates/jit/tests/fast_docs_templates/template_apply_atomicity_tests.rs:179-183`, imports at `:17`; `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/local_rule_enforcement_tests.rs:909-918`). `crates/jit/tests/fast_docs_templates/template_apply_tests.rs` probes presets through storage (`:720,868,979,1001`) and its comments name `PresetManager::new` (`:949,987`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `crate::gate_presets` exports one `pub` catalog constructed from a captured `RepositoryImage`: it derives the preset paths from the `GATE_PRESETS` listing, parses them through `load_presets_from_custom_files`, lists `PresetInfo` sorted by name, and looks a preset up by name, failing with `PresetNotFoundError` when absent. Catalog unit tests over built images own the listing properties: an absent presets directory lists none, the listing is sorted with gate counts, a symlinked or non-file `*.json` occupant is refused, and invalid JSON or a stem mismatch is refused.
- [hard] REQ-02: `capture_gate_preset_image`, `apply_gate_preset`, the template capture and `derive_captured_template_apply` obtain preset paths and presets only through the catalog; `listed_gate_preset_paths`, `parse_captured_gate_presets`, `listed_json_paths` and `parse_template_presets` no longer exist.
- [hard] REQ-03: `list_gate_presets` and `show_gate_preset` capture the `GATE_PRESETS` listing and its `*.json` files in one `with_read_session` closure and answer through the catalog; neither calls an `IssueStore` preset method. A harness test writes the same custom preset files into the in-memory and the JSON-file backends and shows that list and show give equal answers on both, and that the preset `show` reports is the one `apply` attaches.
- [hard] REQ-04: `crates/jit/src/gate_presets/manager.rs` and `PresetManager` no longer exist and the `gate_presets` module rustdoc names the catalog as the reader; `IssueStore` declares no gate-preset method, and neither backend, `gate_presets_from_repository_state`, nor either test wrapper implements or forwards one.
- [hard] REQ-05: The template application tests that probed presets through storage use the executor's preset show and keep their assertions, including that a malformed preset file propagates a parse error rather than `PresetNotFoundError`; the gate preset apply and template apply suites pass unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-06: `docs/reference/storage-format.md` lists `gate preset list` and `gate preset show` among the commands that read through the driver, under the rule `lock-free-read-consumers` states.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: `gate preset list` and `gate preset show` take no repository lock while uncontended and complete a leftover redo record only through the driver's locked fallback. Output is unchanged.
- The catalog names the directory through `VirtualPath::GATE_PRESETS`, never a literal (`@/inv/domain-agnostic`).
- `lock-free-read-consumers`, which this task follows, owns the read-discipline statement in `docs/reference/storage-format.md`; this task adds only its own commands to the list there.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

title: One gate evidence capture resolves its inputs once and enforces the prompt limit
description:
Capture gate evidence for evaluation and for prechecks through one function that also enforces the prompt size limit and resolves the evaluated issue, gate registry and gate definition once per captured image, and delete the precheck variant.

## Background

- Precheck: `captured_precheck_plan` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:659-755`) builds `PrecheckEvidence` (`mod.rs:568-607`) and prompts. It records `VirtualPath::GATES` instead of the gate definitions, reads no issue document or pinned evidence (by `@/issue/8454236c/decision/D-1`; `PrecheckEvidence::matches` compares only paths the image's capture spec holds), parses run records itself (`mod.rs:699-716`), and reads prompt files without a size check (`mod.rs:729-734`). Callers: `publish_captured_lifecycle_mutation` (`mod.rs:2827,2928`) and the test helper `capture_precheck_plan` (`mod.rs:3646-3671`).
- Evaluation: `captured_gate_evaluation` (`crates/jit/src/commands/gate_check.rs:321-425`) builds `GateEvaluationEvidence` (`gate_check.rs:80-91`) with the gate definition, document paths and pinned evidence for exec checkers, run inputs from `captured_gate_runs`, and checks `MAX_PROMPT_FILE_SIZE` (`gate_check.rs:15,385-392`). Callers: `check_gate_with` (`gate_check.rs:949,1005`) and a unit test (`:2624`).
- `build_captured_gate_context` checks the size limit a second time (`gate_check.rs:1273-1280`); for prechecks it is the only check, so an oversized precheck prompt fails only when that gate's context is built, after earlier prechecks have run (`execute_captured_prechecks`, `gate_check.rs:1442`).
- Run history and verdict reuse are read from the captured image: a gate capture holds only the evaluated issue's latest runs, and reuse reads one verdict record.
- `capture_gate_evaluation_image` (`gate_check.rs:762-886`) resolves the bound issue, the registry and the gate (`captured_bound_issue`, `captured_gate_registry`, `required_automated_gate` at `:818-820`) to decide the capture, then returns only `(image, target_id)`.
- `check_gate_with` (`gate_check.rs:902`) resolves all three again from the same image in its inputs attempt (`:930-932`) and looks the gate up a third time in the registry (`:955-958`). Its record session calls `capture_gate_evaluation_image` again and repeats the resolution on that image (`:984-995`).
- Two more functions parsed one image's declarations twice (`captured_issue_rule_report` `:461-462`, `captured_scope_rule_report` `:523-524`); the built-in checkers now select from the one validation report, which removed both.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One function captures gate evidence for one issue and a set of gates (definitions, input identities, run history, pinned evidence where the capture spec holds it, the validation view and prompts); `captured_precheck_plan`'s evidence capture and `captured_gate_evaluation` are replaced by it, and one evidence type replaces `PrecheckEvidence` and `GateEvaluationEvidence`.
- [hard] REQ-02: `MAX_PROMPT_FILE_SIZE` is checked only in that function; `build_captured_gate_context` performs no size check.
- [hard] REQ-03: Precheck evidence still holds no issue document or pinned evidence its mutation base did not capture, and `test_precheck_evidence_detects_prompt_mutation_and_preserves_captured_bytes` (`mod.rs:4356`) passes.
- [hard] REQ-04: A harness test with two auto prechecks, the first of whose checker creates a marker file and the second of whose prompt file exceeds the limit, shows the transition refused with the size-limit error and no marker file created; today the marker exists because the first precheck runs before the second fails.
- [hard] REQ-05: `capture_gate_evaluation_image` returns the captured image together with the bound issue, the parsed gate registry and the gate definition it resolved, `check_gate_with`'s inputs attempt resolves none of them again, and the record session resolves the issue, registry and gate of its own image once, through the same return value, and compares them with the evaluated ones.
- [hard] REQ-06: No function in `gate_check.rs` parses one captured image's declarations or gate registry more than once, and the gate check suites pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: an oversized precheck prompt now refuses the transition at capture, before any precheck runs, instead of when its own context is built. The error text is unchanged.
- The resolve-once change leaves behaviour unchanged.
- `bulk-apply-one-session`, which this task follows, adds a bulk precheck preflight through the shared state derivation; that preflight reaches the evidence capture through `captured_precheck_plan`, so it moves onto the one evidence type here with the lifecycle path.

title: Sessions share the captured image and recognise it by token
description:
Make a captured `RepositoryImage` cheap to share and let a mutation session recognise its own image by an identity token, so neither a capture round nor a materialization plan copies the image and apply never compares it byte for byte.

## Background

- `RepositoryImage` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/image.rs:697-704`) owns its layout, capture spec, entry, listing and pinned-evidence maps, and `CapturedBytes` (`image.rs:104-108`) owns its `Vec<u8>`, so a clone copies every captured byte. `RepositoryImage::close` (`image.rs:708`) builds it; `into_answers` (`image.rs:844-860`) moves the maps out for the next capture round.
- Each capture round keeps a deep copy for the session: `JsonMutationSession::capture_over` sets `self.captured = Some(image.clone())` (`crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store.rs:613`), and `MemoryMutationSession::capture_over` does the same (`:764`). The `captured: Option<RepositoryImage>` fields are at `:410` and `:420`, reset after apply at `:599` and `:750`.
- That copy serves one check only: `ensure_session_image` (`repository_state_store.rs:846-857`), called from both `apply` methods (`:572`, `:731`), refuses a plan unless `captured != Some(image)` is false, a derived byte-for-byte `PartialEq` over the whole image.
- `MaterializationPlan::new` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mod.rs:624-633`, `image: image.clone()` at `:626`) clones the image again into the plan.
- The equality is also what the plan-ownership tests rely on (`test_json_plan_owns_exact_image_and_applies_only_against_it` and `test_memory_plan_owns_exact_image_and_applies_only_against_it`, `crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store_tests.rs:358`, `:393`), and the JSON and memory backends' images are compared for equality (`repository_state_store_tests.rs:2123`).
- Because recognition is by bytes, a plan derived from another session's image applies whenever the two images happen to be byte-identical.
- `dev/architecture/repository-state-materialization.md:143-145` and `:313` describe apply checking that the plan's image is the session's captured image.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A `RepositoryImage` holds its captured data behind shared ownership and an identity token minted by `close`; cloning an image shares both, and `PartialEq` compares captured data only.
- [hard] REQ-02: Capture rounds on both backends retain only the image's token, `MaterializationPlan::new` shares the image it is given, and `extend` reuses the captured maps without copying when no other holder keeps them; a unit test shows a plan's image shares storage with the session's capture.
- [hard] REQ-03: Apply on both backends accepts a plan only when its image carries the session's token. A test that captures byte-identical images in two sessions and applies the first session's plan in the second fails today, because the second session applies it, and passes once the second session refuses it with a retryable conflict.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: a plan built over a byte-identical image captured by another session is refused as a retryable conflict; today it applies. No production path builds a plan from one session's image and applies it in another (preflight images are only read), so commands are unaffected.
- The two architecture-note passages are updated in the same change to say the session recognises its image by token.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Capture rounds and materialization plans share the image without copying, and sessions recognise it by a token.

title: Redo apply opens and syncs each parent once per record
description:
Make redo apply open each distinct parent directory once per record, through a handle map built before the first live write, and use that per-record parent set to decide the directory-sync policy: add the conformance test that shows whether replaying a committed record from any persisted subset of its operations converges, and if it does, sync each distinct parent once per application; otherwise keep per-operation syncs and say why in the module rustdoc.

## Background

- `RedoApplier::apply_operations` (`crates/jit/src/storage/redo_apply.rs:130-179`) first resolves every path through `resolve` (`:196-206`), which walks the parent chain with `open_capability_parent` and discards the handle. Each operation then calls `resolve` again and walks a third time: `make_directory` and `put_file` through `open_or_create_capability_parent` (`:213-226`, `:233-240`), `delete_file` and `append_events` through `open_capability_parent` (`:290-300`, `:308-321`).
- Each walk lstats a component and then `open_child_dir_nofollow` lstats it again before the open (the walks and the open live in `crates/jit/src/storage/capability_fs.rs` once the primitives move there; today `crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store.rs:1552-1641`).
- The pre-pass guarantees that a symlinked or out-of-root ancestor is refused before any live write; `test_redo_applier_apply_refuses_a_path_outside_the_roots_before_any_live_write` (`redo_apply.rs:1036-1064`) owns that property.
- Directory-entry durability needs the directory fsynced. Redo apply syncs the parent after every make-directory, put and delete (`crates/jit/src/storage/redo_apply.rs:217,239,296`) and after each ancestor `open_or_create_capability_parent` creates (in `crates/jit/src/storage/capability_fs.rs` once the primitives move there; today `crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store.rs:1599-1602`). A record whose targets share one parent pays one directory fsync per operation. Coalescing those syncs is safe only if a crash that keeps an arbitrary subset of the unsynced entries still leaves a state the record replays to completion (`@/inv/atomic-writes`).
- The existing matrix (`crates/jit/src/storage/redo_conformance.rs`, `test_the_matrix_drives_an_interruption_at_every_point_on_both_backends` at `:338` and `prop_re_application_after_an_interruption_at_any_point_reaches_and_holds_the_new_state` at `:461`) interrupts in-process, so it reaches only prefixes of the operation sequence: a completed rename stays visible in the page cache. It cannot show convergence from an arbitrary subset.
- Record operations are pairwise path-disjoint (`ensure_disjoint_paths`, `crates/jit/src/storage/redo_record.rs:116-129`, run by `RedoRecord::new` at `:90` and `parse` at `:277`) and each is idempotent (make-directory tolerates a directory, put overwrites through a stage and rename, delete tolerates absence, the append seeks and truncates to offset plus length; `redo_apply.rs:213-321`). That is the argument the test checks.
- The suite's fixtures are `arbitrary_record`, `seed_repository` and `snapshot` from `redo_apply.rs`'s `test_fixtures` (`:379-640`) and the memory fixtures in `crates/jit/src/storage/memory.rs`; `snapshot` sees `.redo.*.tmp` stages that a lost rename leaves, which the orphan sweep owns (`redo_apply.rs:918`).
- The staged file's `sync_all` (`redo_apply.rs:268`) and the event log's `sync_all` (`:320`) are file-data syncs: a rename that persists must name synced bytes, so they stay per operation.
- `RedoApplier::apply` removes the record after `RedoPoint::BeforeRecordRemoval` (`redo_apply.rs:117-127`); `remove_record` syncs the scratch directory (`:325-338`).
- The init publisher (`crates/jit/src/storage/init_publish.rs:51-87`) stages a whole tree, creating ancestors through the syncing walk (`:62`, `:69`), and then runs `sync_tree` (`:134-143`), which syncs every directory again.
- The module rustdoc (`redo_apply.rs:1-8`), `put_file`'s rustdoc (`:228-232`) and `dev/architecture/repository-state-materialization.md:367-368` describe per-put parent syncs.
- Crash model: file data is durable after `sync_all`. A directory entry is durable once its directory's fsync returns; any subset of entries not yet synced may persist. The record is durable before the first live write and removed only after the pass.

- [hard] REQ-01: Redo apply builds one map from (root class, parent directory) to an open handle in its pre-pass, opening each existing ancestor directory once; every operation takes its parent from the map, and an operation that creates a missing ancestor adds it to the map. A unit test applying a record whose targets share ancestors asserts, through the map's per-instance open count, that the count equals the number of distinct ancestor directories; today's applier opens shared ancestors once per walk, so the assertion fails before the change.
- [hard] REQ-02: The pre-pass still refuses a symlinked or out-of-root ancestor before any live write, and the redo conformance matrix passes on both backends.
- [hard] REQ-03: `prop_replay_converges_from_any_subset_of_persisted_operations` in `redo_conformance.rs` runs on both backends: for a generated record of at most seven operations and each subset of them, it seeds the initial state, applies the sub-record of that subset uninterrupted, may create the ancestors of puts outside the subset and may seed event-log residue, then commits and applies the full record and asserts the published state equals a clean application of the full record. The comparison ignores `.redo.*.tmp` stage names, and the test's rustdoc states the crash model it assumes.
- [hard] REQ-04: If the property holds on both backends, it lands in the default suite as the convergence verdict, and redo apply syncs each distinct parent directory in the map that it changed exactly once, after its last operation and before `BeforeRecordRemoval`; staged-file and event-log data syncs stay per operation, and the init publisher creates staged ancestors without per-ancestor syncs and relies on its tree sync. - [hard] REQ-05: If the property fails, it does not land; instead a deterministic test in the same suite applies the shrunk failing record and subset and asserts that replay diverges from clean application, the subset is recorded in the completion evidence, per-operation directory syncs remain, and the module rustdoc states the crash case that requires them. No ignored or failing test lands (`@/inv/no-ignored-tests`).

- Leases are one file per issue, `.git/jit/leases/<issue-id>.json`, named by a `WorktreePaths` constructor, and `.git/jit/claims.seq` holds the last sequence number. The held lease lock's `apply` (`LeaseLock`, `crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs`) publishes a lease change by synced temp file, rename and directory sync (or unlink and directory sync), then bumps `claims.seq`, then appends the operation's history lines in one write. The rename or unlink is the commit point.
- The claims-index writer `write_index_atomic`, with its fixed `claims.index.tmp` stage name, and `jit recover`'s unlocked call to it no longer exist; recovery's lease passes run through the held lease lock.
- An interruption matrix drives `apply` through its failure points and shows an interrupted lease operation leaves the prior or the next lease; it is the owning test for lease crash behaviour.
- Two kinds of control file need the core. The lease records and `claims.seq` live under `.git/jit`, outside every repository root, which the no-follow root opener (`open_absolute_dir_nofollow`, in `storage/capability_fs.rs` after `capability-fs-module`) does not cover, so they need a path entry that opens the target's parent following symlinks. The worktree identity (`<data root>/worktree.json`, `WORKTREE_IDENTITY_FILE`) and the server PID file (`pid_file_path(data_dir)` is `data_dir.join("server.pid.json")`, `crates/jit/src/commands/serve.rs:105-107`, with `data_dir` the `.jit` data root, `crates/jit/src/main.rs:6576, 6634`) live directly in the data root, as the cutover scan records (`crates/jit/tests/scratch_build/repository_state_cutover_tests.rs:660-663`); they can publish through a data-root handle opened no-follow. Repository-state publication stays with the mutation session.
- `write_identity_atomic` (`crates/jit/src/storage/worktree_identity.rs:234-251`) creates a `tempfile::NamedTempFile` beside `worktree.json` (`:240-241`), writes it with `write_file_synced` (`:243`), persists it (`:247`) and syncs the parent through the path-based `sync_directory` (`:250`; both from `crates/jit/src/storage/atomic_write.rs:30,70`, imported at `worktree_identity.rs:7`). Callers: `:163`, `:178`, `:202` and the test at `:341`.
- `write_pid_file` (`crates/jit/src/commands/serve.rs:121-128`) writes `server.pid.pid.tmp`, a fixed name derived by `with_extension("pid.tmp")` (`:123`) from `pid_file_path` (`:105`), with `std::fs::write` and renames it, syncing neither the file nor the directory. Production caller: `start_server` (`:671`). Tests: `test_write_pid_file_is_atomic` (`:845-862`) checks the fixed stage name is gone; `test_start_server_kills_orphan_when_pid_write_fails` (`:1558-1617`) forces the write to fail by placing a directory at that fixed stage name (`:1580`) and checks the orphan through the shared liveness primitive (`:1614`).
- The identity writer is the last caller of `write_file_synced` and of the path-based `sync_directory`.
- The other renames in storage are no-replace publications through `rename_noreplace_cap` (`atomic_write.rs:83,101`; callers `crates/jit/src/storage/external_publish.rs:217` and `crates/jit/src/storage/init_publish.rs:105`), which refuse an occupied destination and are not stage-and-replace writes.
- The storage atomic-write primitives are visible only inside `crate::storage` (`atomic_write.rs:9-14`), so `commands/serve.rs` needs a crate-visible storage entry for its data-root file. A crate-visible entry that wrote any leaf of the data root would be a route around the redo record (`@/inv/derived-state-coherence`, `@/charter/D-17`).
- The repository-state cutover scan (`scan_filesystem_writers`, `crates/jit/tests/scratch_build/repository_state_cutover_tests.rs:819-871`) classifies each function that mutates the filesystem by the markers of `NON_REPOSITORY_WRITES` (`:608-658`: `pid_file_path(` for server process state at `:633`, `WorktreeIdentity` for the identity file at `:638`). A writer no class matches hands the question to its callers when it is not exported, and is reported unclassified when it is `pub fn` or `pub(crate)` (`:744-745`, `:860-867`); a function that calls a classified writer is not a writer itself. `assert_writers_classified` (`:913-930`) fails when a class is no longer seen writing. `OUTSIDE_ROOT_WRITES` (`:664-669`) names the classes whose targets lie outside every root, for the directory-creation scan.
- Other writers keep the two existing classes seen: the server's `remove_pid_file` (`crates/jit/src/commands/serve.rs:131-138`, `pid_file_path(`) and `start_server`'s log open (`:590-605`, `log_file`), and `load_or_create_worktree_identity_with_warnings`, which removes a copied `worktree.json` (`crates/jit/src/storage/worktree_identity.rs:150`) and names `WorktreeIdentity`. Lease storage's functions name `shared_jit`, the claims control plane marker (`crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The core gains a storage-private (`pub(in crate::storage)`) path entry for `.git/jit` control files only, which opens the target's parent following symlinks, creates no directory, and calls the core, with `apply` as its first caller: `apply` publishes a lease record and the `claims.seq` counter through that path entry with full durability, and lease storage contains no stage-and-rename sequence of its own. The entry refuses a target outside the git common directory's `jit` directory and the checkout's own `<git dir>/jit` directory.
- [hard] REQ-02: No lease or claims file is staged under a fixed temporary name. A claim-coordinator unit test shows the wiring: a lease change applied with an injected publication failure leaves the prior lease and no stage file behind, which holds only when the write goes through the shared function (stage-name uniqueness and durability stay owned by that function's own tests). The lease interruption matrix passes unchanged: an interrupted publication leaves the prior or the next lease and a parseable sequence counter.
- [hard] REQ-03: Storage declares a closed control-file type with two values, worktree identity and server PID file. The PID file and a data-root identity publish through one crate-visible entry over a data-root handle opened no-follow; an identity that `identity_file` (`crates/jit/src/storage/worktree_identity.rs`) resolves under `<git dir>/jit` publishes through the REQ-01 entry. Both use full durability and create no directory, and no other path can be passed to either. `write_identity_atomic` and `write_pid_file` publish through these entries; neither names a temporary file, calls `NamedTempFile`, `std::fs::write` or `std::fs::rename`, and a symlinked data root fails the publication.
- [hard] REQ-04: The PID file is synced before `write_pid_file` returns, and a regression test shows a stale `server.pid.pid.tmp` directory no longer fails `write_pid_file` (on today's code the write fails because the stage name is fixed).
- [hard] REQ-05: `test_start_server_kills_orphan_when_pid_write_fails` injects its PID-write failure without relying on a fixed stage name and still proves the orphan is killed.
- [hard] REQ-06: `write_file_synced` and the path-based `sync_directory` no longer exist, nor does any other storage atomic-write helper left without a caller; outside tests, every rename in `crates/jit/src/storage/` and `commands/serve.rs` that replaces a target with a staged file is inside the atomic-publication function, and the remaining renames are `rename_noreplace_cap` publications. `NON_REPOSITORY_WRITES` gains one class, "data-root control file", whose marker is the closed type's name and which the crate-visible entry carries; the class is not listed in `OUTSIDE_ROOT_WRITES`, because its targets sit in the data root and it creates no directory. The "server process state" and "worktree identity" classes stay and stay seen through the writers named in Background, the storage-private `.git/jit` entry carries no class and is classified through its lease callers under "claims control plane", and both cutover scans pass.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged for lease publication: the commit point, the ordering of lease publication, sequence bump and history append, and the on-disk formats stay as they are.
- Behaviour change: the server PID file is durable once `jit serve` reports the server started; a leftover `server.pid.pid.tmp` from a crashed start no longer blocks the next start.

title: Snapshot export copies stored bytes from one image
description:
Name the repository's declaration files once, at the layout, then make snapshot export read the issues it exports and the repository's declaration files from one capture of the repository, and write their stored bytes, so the snapshot holds exactly what the repository holds.

## Background

- Well-known data-root paths are declared once through `declare_well_known_paths!` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/path.rs:291-315`, invoked at `:317-348`): `CONFIG`, `GATES`, `TEMPLATES`, `RULES`, `INVARIANTS` and the `GATE_PRESETS` directory (`config/gate-presets`) among them. `VirtualPath::RECORDS` (`:356`) groups the record paths, but no layout-level name groups the declaration files; the set is implicit.
- The mutation and validation base capture spells the set by hand: `capture_proposed_base_inner` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:331`) discovers `CONFIG, INVARIANTS, RULES, GATES, TEMPLATES` plus `INDEX` at `commands/validate.rs:361-370`.
- The declaration assembly reads the same files from an image: `validation_declarations_from_image` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mod.rs:425`) reads `CONFIG` (`:429`), `TEMPLATES` (`:444`), `GATES` (`:455`) and `RULES` (`:459`), and its config assembly (`assemble_config_from_declarations`, `crates/jit/src/repository_state/materialize.rs`) reads `INVARIANTS`.
- `SnapshotExporter` (`crates/jit/src/commands/snapshot.rs:31-36`) holds `storage`, `worktree_root`, `data_root` and `created_at`; `SnapshotExporter::new` (`:84-97`) takes all four. `CommandExecutor::export_snapshot` builds it at `:683-688`, and the unit-test helper `exporter` does at `:775-782`.
- `enumerate_issues` (`:99-118`) is the only reader of `storage`: it lists or loads issues through `IssueStore` outside any session. Its five unit tests (`test_enumerate_issues_*`, `:785-893`) seed an `InMemoryStorage`.
- `copy_jit_state` (`:447-475`) is the only reader of `data_root` (`:466`). It re-serializes each issue with `serde_json::to_string_pretty` (`:453`) instead of copying its record, and copies only `config.toml` and `gates.toml` (`:462-473`, hand-picked at `:462`) through the shared no-follow repository-file reader in `storage::capability_fs`. Stored records are written by the canonical serializer `serialize_issue` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mutation.rs:545`, keys sorted through `canonicalize_json`), so an exported record differs from the stored one in key order. `rules.toml`, `templates.toml`, `invariants.toml` and `config/gate-presets/` are not exported. `test_copy_jit_state_rejects_malformed_issue_id_without_escape` (`:1042-1050`) exercises the re-serializing path.
- `export_snapshot` calls `assemble` (`:497`, which calls `enumerate_issues` at `:502` and `copy_jit_state` at `:509`) and then publishes through its own session (`publish_repository_export`, `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs`). No captured image exists during assembly.
- `snapshot export` is recovery-dispatched (`crates/jit/src/cli.rs:2897`), so `open_repository` retains a mutation session for the whole command (`crates/jit/src/commands/bootstrap.rs:111-123`), which `main.rs` holds through dispatch (`crates/jit/src/main.rs:1627-1655`); a `with_mutation_session` capture inside the command reenters it. The lock-free read driver is out of scope here (DEC-24). `captured_active_issues` (`commands/mod.rs`) shows how indexed records are read from an image.
- Test constraints: `crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/snapshot_export_tests.rs:80` asserts `.jit/issues` exists in the output, and `test_snapshot_export_rejects_symlinked_data_source_without_output` (`:523-555`) requires a symlinked `.jit/config.toml` to fail the export with no output.

- [hard] REQ-01: `VirtualPath` exposes one declaration set, the declaration files (configuration, gates, templates, rules, invariants) and the declaration directories (the gate-preset directory), each named once in `crates/jit/src/repository_state/path.rs`; `capture_proposed_base_inner` discovers its declaration files through that set with no literal list of those five paths, and a unit test captures an image holding exactly the declaration files plus the index and shows `validation_declarations_from_image` assembles from it without a missing-capture error.
- [hard] REQ-02: Export captures the scope's issue records and the declaration set (files, plus each `*.json` file under the gate-preset directory) in one `with_mutation_session` attempt that returns `SessionStep::Done` without applying a plan, under the session dispatch retains, and assembles the snapshot only from that image; `enumerate_issues` selects over the captured issues, and `SnapshotExporter` no longer has the `storage` and `data_root` fields or their constructor parameters, with `export_snapshot` and the unit-test helper updated.

- The document and asset reads of the export (`read_from_filesystem`, `:175-190`) are unchanged.

title: Archive destinations drop the short-id fallback
description:
Remove the legacy bare-short-id destination from container archive resolution, so a container archives into its marker-backed directory or its preferred directory and nothing else, and state the rule in the adopter reference.

## Background

- `resolve_container_destination` (`crates/jit/src/domain/artifact_classifier.rs:415-485`) takes `legacy_root` (the bare `<archive_root>/<short-id>` directory from `artifact_destination_root`, `:1608-1613`), derives the archive root as its parent (`:421-424`), and falls back to it when no child carries a matching `.jit-container` marker and the legacy directory exists (`:474-482`). `ArtifactEvidenceError::MissingArchiveRoot` (`:406-407`) exists only for that parent derivation.
- The one destination-evidence function in `crates/jit/src/commands/archive.rs` captures the legacy root as evidence for this fallback, and `capture_archive_plan` computes `legacy` from `artifact_destination_root` (`archive.rs:540`).
- `classify_artifacts` (`artifact_classifier.rs:662`) falls back to `artifact_destination_root` when the inventory carries no destination root (`:667-670`); the archive planner always sets one through `with_destination_root`, but the domain discovery builds its inventory without one (`ArtifactClassificationInventory::new` in `discover_archive_artifacts`, `crates/jit/src/domain/artifact_discovery.rs:473`), and the discovery tests classify such inventories directly. Its other callers are `crates/jit/src/commands/archive.rs:302, 826`, the classifier unit tests, and the citation-test helper `plan_with_scan` (`crates/jit/src/storage/artifact_planning.rs:501-532`, call at `:530`), which `archive-preview-through-execute-planner` relocates into `crates/jit/src/storage/artifact_inspection.rs`.

- Data check: the three bare short-id directories under this repository's `dev/archive/` each carry a matching `.jit-container`, so the marker branch already resolves them.
- `docs/reference/cli-commands.md:374-385` says planning resolves to an existing unsuffixed `<archive_root>/<container-short-id>/` directory when no marker matches (`:381-383`). `docs/reference/configuration.md:159` describes the bare short-id directory as the preferred name when no slug resolves; that remains true.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-04: The archive destination section of `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` states marker reuse and the preferred root only.

## Notes

Asserted by REQ-03's test. The adopter description of destination resolution changes in the docs (REQ-04).

title: Domain code reports typed errors and imports nothing from repository_state
description:
Give the proposed-layout check a domain error type, make the artifact classifier's missing-evidence lookup one generic helper, and give every fallible domain parser and constructor a `thiserror` error type, so domain code names nothing in `repository_state`, uses no `anyhow` and returns no bare `String` errors.

title: RootRelativePath lives in the domain with its own parse error
description:
Give `RootRelativePath::parse` an error type of its own, move the type and that error into a pure domain module, point every importer at the domain path, delete the `repository_state` re-export, and assert that the domain layer names nothing in `repository_state`.

## Background

title: Relative path inputs validate through RootRelativePath::parse
description:
Validate declared relative paths in repository inputs, profile packages and storage reads with the one path parser, `RootRelativePath::parse`, and delete the parallel predicates `is_safe_relative_path` and `validate_repo_relative_path` (REQ-20 safe relative paths).

## Background

- `is_safe_relative_path` (`crates/jit/src/domain/repository_inputs.rs:473-490`) checks the same rule as the domain `RootRelativePath::parse`: no backslash, colon, control character, Windows prefix, empty, `.` or `..` segment, or absolute path. They differ only on empty input, which the predicate rejects and the parser maps to the root.
- Callers: `DeclaredRoot::try_from` (`repository_inputs.rs:98-108`, which also admits the worktree root `.`), `validate_relative_path` in `crates/jit/src/profile/package.rs:871-880`, and the tar entry-name check in `crates/jit/src/profile/package_archive.rs:636-646`.
- `has_ordinary_segments` (`repository_inputs.rs:492-497`) stays: the exclusion-pattern shape check still uses it, since patterns admit `:` inside bracket expressions.
- Owning tests: `test_declared_root_rejects_paths_that_cannot_be_joined_to_a_worktree` (`repository_inputs.rs:574`) and the profile package unsafe-path tests.
- `validate_repo_relative_path` (`crates/jit/src/storage/path_errors.rs:57-74`, re-exported at `crates/jit/src/storage/mod.rs:74`) rejects only empty, absolute and `..`-bearing paths.
- `RepositoryLayout::classify_repository_relative` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/path.rs:627-657`) strips any leading `./` (`:636-638`) and then reaches `RootRelativePath::parse` through `VirtualPath::worktree`/`data`, so it refuses `a//b` and `a:b` but accepts `./a`. It has about fifty callers, among them gate prompt resolution (`crates/jit/src/commands/gate_check.rs:375`, `:856`), materialization and profile targets. This repository's `.jit/gates.toml` declares `prompt_file = "./contrib/gates/..."` and `"./scripts/..."` (`:15`, `:152`, `:207`, `:303`, `:414`), and `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:3504-3515` asserts the stripping. That function and its `./` rule stay unchanged.
- The working-tree read entry points check with the lax validator before classifying: `JsonFileStorage::read_repo_file` (`crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:1421-1443`, check at `:1426`) and `InMemoryStorage::repo_file_vpath` (`crates/jit/src/storage/memory.rs:244-252`, check at `:248`). So `read_repo_file("./a")` is accepted today. Production callers of `read_repo_file` pass configured item-kind sources and registries (`crates/jit/src/commands/item.rs:242`, `:273`); this repository's configuration spells none of them with `./`.
- Pinned reads apply only the lax check: `read_path_bytes` with `at_commit` (`json.rs:1456-1512`) validates with `validate_repo_relative_path` (`:1468`) and passes the text to the commit tree lookup, and `validate_path` (`crates/jit/src/storage/git_revision.rs:693-696`; after the git-module consolidation it lives in `crates/jit/src/storage/git.rs`) does the same. They accept `a//b`, `a:b`, `.` segments and backslashes.
- Other callers: `CommandExecutor::add_document` (`crates/jit/src/commands/document.rs:407-410`), `capture_artifact_evidence` (`crates/jit/src/commands/archive.rs:417`, paired with `RootRelativePath::parse`), and `JsonFileStorage::inspect_artifact_location` (`json.rs:692`) while that method exists. The rustdoc of `crates/jit/src/validation/graph.rs:106` names the function.
- Owning storage tests: `test_read_repo_file_present_absent_and_path_safety` (`json.rs:1753`, `memory.rs:1178`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `is_safe_relative_path` no longer exists; its three callers accept a path exactly when `RootRelativePath::parse` returns a descendant, and reject the root (empty input).
- [hard] REQ-02: `validate_repo_relative_path` and its re-export no longer exist. Both backends' `read_repo_file` entry points, the pinned reads and the other listed callers check their argument with `RootRelativePath::parse` (rejecting the root), mapped to `PathReadError::InvalidPath` or the caller's existing invalid-path error; `read_repo_file` checks before classification. `classify_repository_relative` is unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: The declared-root and profile package unsafe-path tests pass unchanged, and the declared-root test adds one case showing empty input is rejected.
- [hard] REQ-04: Both backends' path-safety tests assert that `read_repo_file("./a")` is refused, and the JSON backend's pinned-read test asserts that `a//b` and `a:b` are refused at a commit; each assertion fails today.
- [hard] REQ-05: The `classify_repository_relative` test at `commands/mod.rs:3504-3515` passes unchanged, so `./`-prefixed gate prompt paths still resolve.
- [hard] REQ-06: The `read_repo_file` contract rustdoc (`storage/mod.rs:325-348`) and the `validation/graph.rs` rustdoc name the one parser.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: the `read_repo_file` entry point refuses a leading `./` (a configured item-kind source or registry spelled `./x` is now an invalid path), and pinned reads refuse empty and `.` segments, `:`, `\` and control characters. Every other path input, including gate prompt files and materialization targets, keeps the `./` stripping of `classify_repository_relative`. Asserted by REQ-04 and REQ-05.
- Declared relative paths in repository inputs and profile packages behave as before: every input accepted or rejected before is accepted or rejected now.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

title: Link checks and snapshot export select issues through one IssueScope
description:
Add one domain scope type for selecting issues (`all`, one issue, or one label) with one parser and one selection function, switch `jit doc check-links` and `jit snapshot export` to it with the issue prefix resolved at CLI entry, and delete `DocumentScope` and `SnapshotScope` (REQ-20 scope type).

## Background

- Two types express one selection grammar today. `DocumentScope` (`crates/jit/src/document/scope.rs:23`, `All` and `Issue(String)`, parse error `DocumentScopeParseError` at `:13`) serves `jit doc check-links`. `SnapshotScope` (`crates/jit/src/snapshot.rs:141-187`, `All`, `Issue(String)`, `Label { namespace, value }`, with an `anyhow` `parse` at `:152` and `Display` at `:179`) serves `jit snapshot export`.
- A scope names an issue by a possibly short prefix: check-links resolves it through `IssueIdPrefix::parse` and `resolve_issue_id` (`crates/jit/src/commands/document.rs:1114-1120`), and the short-prefix harness case is `crates/jit/tests/fast_issue/short_hash_tests.rs:281`. `IssueIdPrefix` and its typed `InvalidIdPrefixError` live in `crates/jit/src/domain/issue_id.rs:19,42`; the output classifier already maps that error to the argument exit class (`crates/jit/src/output/failure.rs:289-302`). The parsed scope therefore cannot hold a full `IssueId`; the caller resolves the prefix at CLI entry and then selects.
- `DocumentScope` and `DocumentScopeParseError` (`document/scope.rs:13-50`, unit tests `:53-88`) are re-exported at `crates/jit/src/document/mod.rs:27` (module at `:13`). The module rustdoc (`scope.rs:3`) cites `SnapshotScope` as its pattern.
- The check-links CLI arm parses at `crates/jit/src/main.rs:5065-5072` and calls `CommandExecutor::check_document_links(&DocumentScope)` (`crates/jit/src/commands/document.rs:1098-1360`, which already carries the `RepositoryStateStore` bound), which resolves `Issue(prefix)` with `IssueIdPrefix::parse` and `resolve_issue_id` and lists all issues for `All`. `DocumentScope::Issue("")` is accepted by the parser today (`scope.rs:84`). The invalid-argument exit class for a bad scope comes from the downcast at `crates/jit/src/output/failure.rs:315`. The help text reads "Scope of validation (all or issue:ID)" (`crates/jit/src/cli.rs:1828`). The short-prefix harness row calls `check_document_links(&DocumentScope::Issue(short))` (`short_hash_tests.rs:101,281`). CLI tests are in `crates/jit/tests/cli_query_graph/check_links_tests.rs`.
- `SnapshotScope` tests are `test_scope_parse_*` (`snapshot.rs:253-330`). Consumers: the CLI arm (`main.rs:7247-7251`), `crates/jit/src/commands/snapshot.rs` (import `:8`, `enumerate_issues` `:99-118` with its label matching, `:291`, `:499`, `:672`, unit tests `:795-895`), the help text (`cli.rs:2293`) and the rustdoc list in `crates/jit/src/validation/graph.rs:86`. Snapshot export reads its issues from one captured image, so selection is a pure function over the captured issues. The manifest records the scope as text (`SnapshotManifest::scope`, `snapshot.rs:23`).
- `docs/reference/cli-commands.md:2823-2845` documents `jit doc check-links [--scope all|issue:<ID>]` (`:2828`); the scope grammar snapshot export documents is at `:3577`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A domain `IssueScope<I>` with `All`, `Issue(I)` and `Label { namespace, value }` exists in `crates/jit/src/domain/issue_scope.rs`; `FromStr` for `IssueScope<IssueIdPrefix>` accepts `all`, `issue:<prefix>` and `label:<namespace>:<value>` with a typed error, `Display` round-trips, one method maps the parsed scope to `IssueScope<IssueId>` through a caller-supplied resolver, and one pure function returns the issues an `IssueScope<IssueId>` admits from a slice of issues.
- [hard] REQ-02: The module's unit tests own the parse cases (all, issue prefix, too-short prefix, label, label with a colon in the value, malformed label, unknown form), the round-trip and the selection cases.
- [hard] REQ-03: `DocumentScope`, `DocumentScopeParseError`, `document/scope.rs` and `SnapshotScope` with its parse tests no longer exist; both CLI arms parse `--scope` as `IssueScope<IssueIdPrefix>` and resolve the prefix at entry, `check_document_links` takes `IssueScope<IssueId>`, and link checks and snapshot export select with the domain selection function, with no scope parsing or label matching left in `commands/snapshot.rs`.
- [hard] REQ-04: An invalid scope keeps the invalid-argument exit class, a too-short or ambiguous prefix keeps its prefix error class, the short-prefix harness row resolves through the same entry resolution, the snapshot manifest's `scope` text is the scope's `Display` for each form, and the snapshot export tests pass.
- [hard] REQ-05: A CLI test running `jit doc check-links --scope label:<namespace>:<value>` checks only the documents of issues carrying that label; it fails today because the scope is rejected.
- [hard] REQ-06: `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` names the `label:<namespace>:<value>` scope in the check-links synopsis and text, stated once and linked from the snapshot export section, which does not restate the grammar.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: link checks accept `label:<namespace>:<value>`, and the CLI help names the three forms. Asserted by REQ-05; the adopter reference is updated by REQ-06.
- `issue:` with an empty or too-short prefix now fails at parse with the prefix error instead of at resolution; the exit class is the same.
- Snapshot export is otherwise unchanged, except that a short issue prefix in `issue:<prefix>` resolves like every other command's prefix.

title: Process liveness and signalling go through one PID guard
description:
Give the crate one process-liveness probe and one PID guard, so every liveness check and signal site converts PIDs the same `@/inv/pid-safety` way, a live process owned by another user reads as alive, and non-unix platforms follow one policy (REQ-20 process liveness).

## Background

- Two liveness primitives disagree: `is_process_alive` (`crates/jit/src/commands/serve.rs:154-175`, non-unix `false`) and `process_exists` (`crates/jit/src/storage/lock_cleanup.rs:15-44`, non-unix `true`). Both read `kill(pid, 0).is_ok()`, so a live process owned by another user, for which `kill` fails with `EPERM`, reads as dead. `cleanup_stale_locks` (`lock_cleanup.rs:67`, check at `:112`) therefore removes a lock a live foreign process holds.
- Each primitive carries its own copy of the PID guard (checked `u32` to `i32` conversion, positive value): `serve.rs:162-167` and `lock_cleanup.rs:27-30`.
- Liveness callers, all in `serve.rs`: `start_server` (`:571`), `run_foreground` (`:701`), `stop_server` (`:751`) and `server_status` (`:794`); serve tests `:1494`, `:1527`, `:1614`. `main.rs` reaches liveness only through these functions. Duplicated primitive tests: `serve.rs:904-921` and `lock_cleanup.rs:150-176`.
- `stop_server` (`serve.rs:749-786`) converts the PID with its own `i32::try_from` (`:767-768`) before sending `SIGTERM` (`:773-774`).
- `kill_process_group` (`crates/jit/src/gate_execution.rs:321-337`, unix) negates a checked `i32` and sends `SIGKILL` to the group (`:330-332`), refusing PIDs at or below 1, because `kill(-1)` signals every process the user owns and `kill(0)` the caller's own group; the non-unix variant (`:341-343`) only kills the child.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A crate module `crates/jit/src/process.rs` owns the PID guard and the liveness probe; `is_process_alive` and `process_exists` no longer exist, and every liveness caller listed above uses the probe.
- [hard] REQ-02: The probe reports a process alive when the probe succeeds or fails with `EPERM`, dead only on `ESRCH` or a guard refusal, and alive on non-unix platforms. A regression test shows the probe outcome `EPERM` maps to alive (on today's code `kill(pid, 0).is_ok()` maps it to dead), independent of the user the suite runs as.
- [hard] REQ-03: The new module's own tests own the current-process, invalid-PID, `u32::MAX` and PID-0 cases; the copies in `serve.rs` and `lock_cleanup.rs` are gone.
- [hard] REQ-04: `stop_server` and `kill_process_group` convert PIDs only through the guard in `process.rs`; neither calls `i32::try_from` on a PID itself.
- [hard] REQ-05: The guard offers a process-group conversion that refuses PID 0 and PID 1 as well as non-positive and overflowing values, and `kill_process_group` falls back to killing the child when it refuses, as today.
- [hard] REQ-06: Unit tests in `process.rs` own the group-target refusals (0, 1, `u32::MAX`) and the accepted case; `stop_server` with a PID the guard refuses reports an error and sends no signal.

## Notes

- Behaviour changes: `cleanup_stale_locks` keeps a lock whose holder is a live process owned by another user; `jit serve` start, status and stop treat another user's live PID as running; on non-unix platforms the server liveness check reports alive (it reported dead), so a stale PID file there no longer starts a duplicate server.
- The signal sites signal or refuse the same PIDs as today.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: One guarded liveness probe, EPERM and non-unix alive, serves every liveness check and signal site (REQ-20).

title: Type labels have one exact extraction
description:
Read type labels through one extractor that returns the exact label value, and delete the lowercasing `extract_type`, so the taxonomy check and the graph and validation code agree on what a type label names (REQ-20 type extraction).

## Background

- `crate::labels::type_value_of` (`crates/jit/src/labels.rs:169-176`) is documented as the one primitive that owns the `type:` encoding and returns the value unchanged. The label grammar allows uppercase values.
- `extract_type` (`crates/jit/src/domain/type_taxonomy.rs:173-180`) wraps it and lowercases and trims the value. Its callers are `detect_validation_issues` (`type_taxonomy.rs:267`, use at `:280`), `validate_strategic_labels` (`:306`, use at `:315`) and `validate_orphans` (`:355`, use at `:364`), plus tests (`test_extract_type_valid` `:472-484`, `test_extract_type_invalid_format` `:487-496`, `prop_extract_type_normalization` `:694-706`, `prop_invalid_labels_rejected` `:710-718`); the module has no rustdoc example. Nothing outside the module calls it.
- So `type:Epic` is the known type `epic` to the taxonomy check and the membership warnings but an unknown type to graph and validation code built on `type_value_of`.
- An unknown type already carries an edit-distance suggestion (`suggest_type_fix`, `:228`), which offers `epic` for `Epic`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `extract_type` no longer exists; `detect_validation_issues`, `validate_strategic_labels` and `validate_orphans` read the type through `type_value_of` and compare the exact value.
- [hard] REQ-02: A unit test shows `detect_validation_issues` reports `type:Epic`, against a hierarchy declaring `epic`, as an unknown type `Epic` with the suggested fix `epic`; today it reports no issue.
- [hard] REQ-03: The extraction tests use `type_value_of` or are removed where `labels.rs` tests already own the extraction property.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: an uppercase type value is an unknown type to the taxonomy check and the strategic and orphan membership warnings, as it already is to graph rules and validation; `validate --fix` offers the lowercase type through the existing suggestion.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
